Saudi suspect detained.wikitext:
Police took a 20-year-old Saudi national into custody near the scene of the Boston Marathon bomb attack.<ref>[http://www.nypost.com/p/news/national/fbi_grills_saudi_man_XaT5rE40LDdAH44vMFOEXM  "FBI grills Saudi man in Boston bombings", New York Daily Post, April 16, 2013.]</ref> The potential suspect was questioned by the FBI and local police at Boston’s Brigham and Women’s Hospital, where he was under heavy guard while being treated for shrapnel injuries to his leg sustained in the blast.<ref>[http://www.nypost.com/p/news/national/fbi_grills_saudi_man_XaT5rE40LDdAH44vMFOEXM  "FBI grills Saudi man in Boston bombings", New York Daily Post, April 16, 2013.]</ref>

In late afternoon, a large group of federal and state law enforcement agents raided an apartment in a building in the Saudi man’s hometown of Revere, Mass.<ref>[http://www.nypost.com/p/news/national/fbi_grills_saudi_man_XaT5rE40LDdAH44vMFOEXM  "FBI grills Saudi man in Boston bombings", New York Daily Post, April 16, 2013.]</ref>
Saudi suspect detained.plaintext:
Police took a 20-year-old Saudi national into custody near the scene of the Boston Marathon bomb attack. "FBI grills Saudi man in Boston bombings", New York Daily Post, April 16, 2013. The potential suspect was questioned by the FBI and local police at Boston’s Brigham and Women’s Hospital, where he was under heavy guard while being treated for shrapnel injuries to his leg sustained in the blast. "FBI grills Saudi man in Boston bombings", New York Daily Post, April 16, 2013.

In late afternoon, a large group of federal and state law enforcement agents raided an apartment in a building in the Saudi man’s hometown of Revere, Mass. "FBI grills Saudi man in Boston bombings", New York Daily Post, April 16, 2013.

MIT shooting.wikitext:
A shooting occurred on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near Building 32 ([[Stata Center]]), at 10:48 p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EDT]] ([[UTC−04:00]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html|publisher=Boston Globe|title=Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013|authors=Wesley Lowery, Eric Moskowitz, Lisa Wangsness}}</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>[http://emergency.mit.net/emergency MIT Emergency Information] April 19, 2013</ref> It was subsequently reported that an MIT police officer received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown [[Boston]], where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=cnn1>{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/18/us/cambridge-gunshots/index.html|publisher=CNN|title=Officer killed on MIT campus near Boston|accessdate=April 19, 2013|date=April 19, 2013|author=Ben Brumfield}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Police in [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]] reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |work=The New York Times }}</ref> Explosions and automatic weapon fire were heard.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston - Adam Clark Estes |publisher=The Atlantic Wire |date= |accessdate=2013-04-19}}</ref> MIT's emergency alerts advised students to stay indoors, and that the suspect may be on campus, until around 2:00AM local time.<ref name="MIT news office">{{citation |url=http://web.mit.edu/newsoffice/2013/campus-shooting-officer-killed-0419.html |title=MIT Police Officer dies in line of duty; MIT Police determine campus to be safe |work=MIT News }}</ref>

The gunmen were reportedly the suspects in the [[Boston Marathon bombings]].<ref>http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html</ref>

During the morning of April 19th, after a car chase, one suspect was captured, while another was still being searched for in the Watertown/Cambridge area.<ref name=Lowery>{{cite web|last=Lowery|first=Wesley|title=One suspect in custody, another remains on the loose|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html|publisher=The Boston Globe|accessdate=19 April 2013|date=19|month=April|year=2013}}</ref> It is unknown if they were part of the shooting death of a police officer at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] or the robbery of two convenience stores nearby.

Police in [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]] reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |work=The New York Times |postscript=<!-- Bot inserted parameter. MIT shooting and arrest.plaintext:
A shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center), at 10:48 p.m. EDT (UTC−04:00) on April 18, 2013. Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 It was subsequently reported that an MIT police officer received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, local news station WBZ estimating that at least 60-70 rounds had been fired, first from rifles and then from handguns. Explosions and automatic weapon fire were heard. MIT's emergency alerts advised students to stay indoors, and later determined at 2 a.m. local time that the campus was safe. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase, one suspect (identified as Suspect 1 on police logs) was described by the police as "accounted for", and by media outlets as either captured or killed, while another was still being sought in the Watertown/Cambridge area. The Boston Globe has quoted "an official with knowledge of the investigation" as saying that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece Watertown resident Andrew Kitzenberg told MSNBC in an interview that he had seen one of the suspects use an explosive device in the firefight, and that he had seen one of them "go down" after charging the police while firing, either tackled or shot. Several sources report a suspect was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody. http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.htmlhttp://www.sfgate.com/business/bloomberg/article/Mayhem-Erupts-in-Boston-as-MIT-Campus-Police-4447027.php

On April 18, a shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). During the morning of April 19, after a car chase, one suspect (referred to as "suspect number one" or "the black-hat suspect") was described by the police as "accounted for", and by media outlets as either captured or killed, while another was still being sought in the Watertown/Cambridge area. The Boston Globe has quoted "an official with knowledge of the investigation" as saying that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Watertown resident Andrew Kitzenberg told MSNBC in an interview that he had seen one of the suspects use an explosive device in the firefight, and that he had seen one of them "go down" after charging the police while firing, either tackled or shot. Several sources report a suspect was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody. 

At an impromptu police press conference, law enforcement officials confirmed that "suspect number one" died at the hospital, and "suspect number two" (the "white-hat suspect") is "still at large".

On April 18, a [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology shooting|shooting]] occurred on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near Building 32 ([[Stata Center]]) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html|publisher=Boston Globe|title=Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013|author=Wesley Lowery, Eric Moskowitz, Lisa Wangsness}}</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>[http://emergency.mit.net/emergency MIT Emergency Information] April 19, 2013</ref> It was subsequently reported that an MIT police officer received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=cnn1>{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/18/us/cambridge-gunshots/index.html|publisher=CNN|title=Officer killed on MIT campus near Boston|accessdate=April 19, 2013|date=April 19, 2013|author=Ben Brumfield}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Police in [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]] reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times }}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston |author=Adam Clark Estes |publisher=The Atlantic Wire |date=|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''The [[Boston Globe]]'' would report that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery"/> 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase, one suspect (referred to as "suspect number one" or "the black-hat suspect") was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of injuries.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie |agency=Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title=Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last=Philippe Naughton|first=Philippe|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Several sources report that a suspect was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody.<ref name="Brumfield">{{cite web|url=http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html|title=Boston bombing suspect on the loose, police say|last=Brumfield|first=Ben|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Linskey">{{cite web|url=http://www.sfgate.com/business/bloomberg/article/Mayhem-Erupts-in-Boston-as-MIT-Campus-Police-4447027.php|title=Mayhem Erupts in Boston as MIT Campus Police Officer Slain|last=Linskey|first=Annie|coauthors=Brian K. Sullivan and Stephen Merelman|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The second suspect, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news|author=CBS / Associated Press|title=1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/|accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url=http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place".<ref>{{cite news|last=Murphy|first=Shelley|title=Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html|accessdate=19 April 2013|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=19 April 2013|location=Boston}}</ref>
MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
On April 18, a shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 It was subsequently reported that an MIT police officer received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe would report that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase, one suspect (referred to as "suspect number one" or "the black-hat suspect") was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of injuries.The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Several sources report that a suspect was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody.

The second suspect, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place".

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase, one suspect (referred to as "suspect number one" or "the black-hat suspect") was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of injuries. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Several sources report that a suspect was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody.

The second suspect, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place".

Valencia, Wesley Lowery, Akilah Johnson, Eric Moskowitz, Lisa Wangsness and John R. Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>[http://emergency.mit.net/emergency MIT Emergency Information] April 19, 2013</ref> It was subsequently reported that an MIT police officer received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=cnn1>{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/18/us/cambridge-gunshots/index.html|publisher=CNN|title=Officer killed on MIT campus near Boston|accessdate=April 19, 2013|date=April 19, 2013|author=Ben Brumfield}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Police in [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]] reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times }}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston |author=Adam Clark Estes |publisher=The Atlantic Wire |date=|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''The [[Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery"/> 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of injuries.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie |agency=Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title=Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last=Philippe Naughton|first=Philippe|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Several sources report that a suspect was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody.<ref name="Brumfield">{{cite web|url=http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html|title=Boston bombing suspect on the loose, police say|last=Brumfield|first=Ben|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Linskey">{{cite web|url=http://www.sfgate.com/business/bloomberg/article/Mayhem-Erupts-in-Boston-as-MIT-Campus-Police-4447027.php|title=Mayhem Erupts in Boston as MIT Campus Police Officer Slain|last=Linskey|first=Annie|coauthors=Brian K. Sullivan and Stephen Merelman|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The second suspect, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news|author=CBS / Associated Press|title=1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/|accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url=http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "[[shelter in place]]". MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
On April 18, a shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 It was subsequently reported that an MIT police officer received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of injuries. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Several sources report that a suspect was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody.

The second suspect, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire MBTA network was suspended as a result.

Suspects.plaintext: On April 18 at around 5:20 P.M. EDT, the FBI released in a news conference photos and a video of two suspects and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded.

Suspects.plaintext: On April 18 at around 5:20 P.M. EDT, the FBI released in a news conference photos and a video of two suspects and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Authorities identified two brothers, 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnayev and 19 year old Dzhokhar Tsarnayev, as suspects--both immigrants of Chechen background originally from the Russian Caucasus region.

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
On April 18, a shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired;MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 an MIT police officer received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of injuries. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Several sources report that a suspect was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody.

The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended as a result. Logan Airport remains open.

The morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended as a result. Logan Airport remains open.

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
On April 18, a shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of injuries. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Several sources report that an individual was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody.

The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended as a result. Logan Airport remains open.

Suspects.plaintext: On April 18 at around 5:20 P.M. EDT, the FBI released in a news conference photos and a video of two suspects and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Authorities identified two brothers, 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnayev (Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnayev (Джохар Царнаев), as suspects. Chechens from the Russian Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in c. 2000–2001. Tamerlan Tsarnaev, who presented himself as a devout Muslim, was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev posted links to websites about Islam and Chechen separatism on his page on a social networking service.

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
On April 18, a shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of injuries. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Several sources report that an individual was surrounded by police and ordered to strip completely naked before being arrested and taken into custody.

The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended as a result. Logan Airport remains open.

According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Authorities identified two brothers, 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnayev (Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnayev (Джохар Царнаев), as suspects. Chechens from the Russian Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2000 or 2001. Tamerlan Tsarnaev, who presented himself as a devout Muslim, was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev posted links to websites about Islam and Chechen separatism on his page on a social networking service.

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
On April 18, a shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. The officer was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of injuries. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended as a result. Logan Airport remains open.

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
On April 18, a shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of injuries. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended as a result. Logan Airport remains open.

Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>[http://emergency.mit.net/emergency MIT Emergency Information] April 19, 2013</ref> Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26|author=Haven, Stephanie|date=April 19, 2013|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news|title=Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author=Seelye, Katherine Q. and Cooper, Michael|date=April 19, 2013|work=The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They then released the man when the ATM cash limit was reached.  Policed chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts <ref>http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html</ref>

Police in [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]] reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times }}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston |author=Adam Clark Estes |publisher=The Atlantic Wire |date=|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery"/> 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of injuries.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie |agency=Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title=Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last=Philippe Naughton|first=Philippe|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news|author=CBS / Associated Press|title=1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/|accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url=http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "[[shelter in place]]". On April 18, a shooting occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They then released the man when the ATM cash limit was reached.  Policed chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

During the morning of April 19, after a car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of injuries. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended as a result. Logan Airport remains open.

thumb|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the remaining, living suspect in the bombingsIn a news conference held at around 5:20 p.m. on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Authorities identified two brothers, 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev () and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (), as suspects. Chechens from the Russian Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2000 or 2001.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (born October 21, 1986), who presented himself as a devout Muslim, was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) posted links to websites about Islam and Chechen separatism on his page on VKontakte, a Russian social networking service. On his page, he listed his languages as English, Russian and Chechen; his worldview was given as "Islam". According to his VKontakte account, he graduated from School No. 1 in Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia in 2001, and graduated from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School in 2011. He received a $2,500 scholarship to attend college from the city of Cambridge the year he graduated; he had also been named a wrestling all-star the same year.

According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Authorities identified two brothers, 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev () and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (), as suspects. Chechens from the Russian Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2000 or 2001.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev ( - )http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Boston-Marathon-Bombing-Suspects-JFK-NYC-Travel-International-203787721.html?_osource=SocialFlowTwt_NYBrand, who presented himself as a devout Muslim, was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev () posted links to websites about Islam and Chechen separatism on his page on VKontakte, a Russian social networking service. On his page, he listed his languages as English, Russian and Chechen; his worldview was given as "Islam". According to his VKontakte account, he graduated from School No. 1 in Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia in 2001, and graduated from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School in 2011. He received a $2,500 scholarship to attend college from the city of Cambridge the year he graduated; he had also been named a wrestling all-star the same year.

On April 18, one of the suspects was photographed in a 7-Eleven in Cambridge, MA, apparently attempting to rob it for cash.  http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-504083_162-57580402-504083/boston-marathon-bombings-timeline-of-events-in-the-manhunt-for-bombing-suspects/

A shooting then occurred on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They then released the man when the ATM cash limit was reached. The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Policed chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured, the other managed to escape with the S.U.V.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds. On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended as a result. Logan Airport remains open.

On April 18, one of the suspects was photographed in a [[7-Eleven]] in Cambridge, apparently attempting to rob it for cash.  <ref>http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-504083_162-57580402-504083/boston-marathon-bombings-timeline-of-events-in-the-manhunt-for-bombing-suspects/</ref>

A shooting then occurred on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near Building 32 ([[Stata Center]]) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html|publisher=Boston Globe|title=Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013|author=Shelley Murphy, Milton J. Valencia, Wesley Lowery, Akilah Johnson, Eric Moskowitz, Lisa Wangsness and John R. Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>[http://emergency.mit.net/emergency MIT Emergency Information] April 19, 2013</ref> Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26|author=Haven, Stephanie|date=April 19, 2013|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news|title=Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author=Seelye, Katherine Q. and Cooper, Michael|date=April 19, 2013|work=The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They then released the man when the ATM cash limit was reached. Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>[http://emergency.mit.net/emergency MIT Emergency Information] April 19, 2013</ref> Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26|author=Haven, Stephanie|date=April 19, 2013|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news|title=Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author=Seelye, Katherine Q. and Cooper, Michael|date=April 19, 2013|work=The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Police in [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]] reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times }}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston |author=Adam Clark Estes |publisher=The Atlantic Wire |date=|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery"/> 

A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the S.U.V.  A transit police officer was critically wounded.<ref name=nytdragnet/>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and an explosion.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie |agency=Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title=Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last=Philippe Naughton|first=Philippe|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news|author=CBS / Associated Press|title=1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/|accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url=http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan Airport]] remains open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." The father said, "If they killed him, then all hell would break loose."<ref>April 19, 2013, [http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ "Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies"], ABC News, Retrieved April 19, 2013</ref>
MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
On April 18, one of the suspects was photographed in a 7-Eleven in Cambridge, apparently attempting to rob it for cash.  http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-504083_162-57580402-504083/boston-marathon-bombings-timeline-of-events-in-the-manhunt-for-bombing-suspects/

A shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached. The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Policed chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the S.U.V.  A transit police officer was critically wounded.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and an explosion. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. 

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." The father said, "If they killed him, then all hell would break loose."April 19, 2013, "Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies", ABC News, Retrieved April 19, 2013

Classmates described him as a kind, sociable individual who was well-integrated into his school community and was "more relaxed" in contrast to his elder brother. He received a $2,500 scholarship to attend college from the city of Cambridge the year he graduated; he had also been named a wrestling all-star the same year. On April 18, one of the suspects was photographed in a [[7-Eleven]] in Cambridge, apparently attempting to rob it for cash.  <ref>http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-504083_162-57580402-504083/boston-marathon-bombings-timeline-of-events-in-the-manhunt-for-bombing-suspects/</ref>

A shooting followed on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near Building 32 ([[Stata Center]]) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html|publisher=Boston Globe|title=Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013|author=Shelley Murphy, Milton J. Valencia, Wesley Lowery, Akilah Johnson, Eric Moskowitz, Lisa Wangsness and John R. Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>[http://emergency.mit.net/emergency MIT Emergency Information] April 19, 2013</ref> Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26|author=Haven, Stephanie|date=April 19, 2013|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news|title=Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author=Seelye, Katherine Q. and Cooper, Michael|date=April 19, 2013|work=The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached. The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and the MIT shooting.<ref name=nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author= |url= http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |work= |date=19 April 2013}}</ref> Policed chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html |title=Bombing manhunt locks down Boston |publisher=CNN.com |date=2012-09-11 |accessdate=2013-04-19}}</ref>

Police in [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]] reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times }}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston |author=Adam Clark Estes |publisher=The Atlantic Wire |date=|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery"/> 

A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the S.U.V.  A transit police officer was critically wounded.<ref name=nytdragnet/>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and an explosion.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie |agency=Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title=Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last=Philippe Naughton|first=Philippe|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news|author=CBS / Associated Press|title=1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/|accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url=http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> 

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan Airport]] remains open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]], encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." A shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and the MIT shooting. Policed chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.

A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the S.U.V.  A transit police officer was critically wounded.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and an explosion. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon. 

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." The father said, "If they killed him, then all hell would break loose."April 19, 2013, "Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies", ABC News, Retrieved April 19, 2013

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the remaining, living suspect in the bombingsIn a news conference held at around 5:20 p.m. on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Authorities identified two brothers, 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev () and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev<ref name=”AtlanticWire04192013”> (), as suspects. Chechens from the Russian Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2000 or 2001.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (),http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Boston-Marathon-Bombing-Suspects-JFK-NYC-Travel-International-203787721.html?_osource=SocialFlowTwt_NYBrand who presented himself as a devout Muslim, was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev () posted links to websites about Islam and Chechen separatism on his page on VKontakte, a Russian social networking service. On his page, he listed his languages as English, Russian and Chechen; his worldview was given as "Islam" and his personal priority was "career and money". According to his VKontakte account, he attended School No. 1 in Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia, in 2001, and graduated from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School in 2011. Classmates and acquaintances described him as a kind, sociable individual who was well-integrated into his school community and was "very relaxed" in contrast to his elder brother. He received a $2,500 scholarship to attend college from the city of Cambridge the year he graduated; he had also been named a wrestling all-star the same year.  At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth with a major in marine biology.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the surviving 19-year-old suspect in the bombingsIn a news conference held at around 5:20 p.m. on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Authorities identified two brothers, 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev () and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev  (), as suspects. Chechens from the Russian Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2000 or 2001.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (),http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Boston-Marathon-Bombing-Suspects-JFK-NYC-Travel-International-203787721.html?_osource=SocialFlowTwt_NYBrand who presented himself as a devout Muslim, was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev () posted links to websites about Islam and Chechen separatism on his page on VKontakte, a Russian social networking service. On his page, he listed his languages as English, Russian and Chechen; his worldview was given as "Islam" and his personal priority was "career and money". According to his VKontakte account, he attended School No. 1 in Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia, in 2001, and graduated from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School in 2011. Classmates and acquaintances described him as a kind, sociable individual who was well-integrated into his school community and was "very relaxed." He received a $2,500 scholarship to attend college from the city of Cambridge the year he graduated; he had also been named a wrestling all-star the same year.  At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth with a major in marine biology.

According to his VKontakte account, he attended School No. 1 in Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia, in 2001, and graduated from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School in 2011. He received a $2,500 scholarship to attend college from the city of Cambridge the year he graduated; he had also been named a wrestling all-star the same year.  At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth with a major in marine biology.

A shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached. The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and the MIT shooting. Policed chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the S.U.V.  A transit police officer was critically wounded.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and an explosion. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",, or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon. 

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." The father said, "If they killed him, then all hell would break loose."April 19, 2013, "Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies", ABC News, Retrieved April 19, 2013

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the surviving 19-year-old suspectIn a news conference held at around 5:20 p.m. on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Authorities identified two brothers, 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev () and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev  (), as suspects. Chechens from the Russian Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2000 or 2001.  They have been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts for the last year.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013),http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Boston-Marathon-Bombing-Suspects-JFK-NYC-Travel-International-203787721.html?_osource=SocialFlowTwt_NYBrand who presented himself as a devout Muslim, was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) posted links to websites about Islam and Chechen separatism on his page on VKontakte, a Russian social networking service. On his page, he listed his languages as English, Russian and Chechen; his worldview was given as "Islam" and his personal priority was "career and money". According to his VKontakte account, he attended School No. 1 in Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia, in 2001, and graduated from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School in 2011. Classmates and acquaintances described him as a kind, sociable individual who was well-integrated into his school community and was "very relaxed." He received a $2,500 scholarship to attend college from the city of Cambridge the year he graduated; he had also been named a wrestling all-star the same year.  At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth with a major in marine biology.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the 19-year-old suspect currently at largeIn a news conference held at around 5:20 p.m. on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the men pictured was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Authorities identified two brothers, 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev () and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev  (), as suspects. Chechens from the Russian Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2000 or 2001.  They have been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the last year.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013),http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Boston-Marathon-Bombing-Suspects-JFK-NYC-Travel-International-203787721.html?_osource=SocialFlowTwt_NYBrand who presented himself as a devout Muslim, was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) posted links to websites about Islam and Chechen separatism on his page on VKontakte, a Russian social networking service. On his page, he listed his languages as English, Russian and Chechen; his worldview was given as "Islam" and his personal priority was "career and money". According to his VKontakte account, he attended School No. 1 in Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia, in 2001, and graduated from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School in 2011. Classmates and acquaintances described him as a kind, sociable individual who was well-integrated into his school community and was "very relaxed." He received a $2,500 scholarship to attend college from the city of Cambridge the year he graduated; he had also been named a wrestling all-star the same year.  At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth with a major in marine biology.

A shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.MIT Emergency Information April 19, 2013 Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached. The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and the MIT shooting. Policed chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.

Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. 

A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the S.U.V.  A transit police officer was critically wounded.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and an explosion. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon. 

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked the entire city of Boston and nearby communities to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." The father said, "If they killed him, then all hell would break loose."April 19, 2013, "Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies", ABC News, Retrieved April 19, 2013
