MIT shooting and Watertown incident.wikitext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near Building 32 ([[Stata Center]]) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web|url = http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |publisher=Boston Globe|title= Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1 =Shelley | last1 = Murphy | first2 = Milton J | last2 = Valencia | first3 = Wesley | last3 = Lowery | first4 = Akilah | last4 = Johnson | first5 = Eric | last5 = Moskowitz | first6 = Lisa | last6 = Wangsness | first7 = John R | last7 = Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://emergency.mit.net/emergency | publisher = MIT | title = Emergency Information | date = April 19, 2013}}.</ref> Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven | first = Stephanie|date = April 19, 2013|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url = http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds.<ref name = SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye | first1 = Katherine Q | last2 = Cooper | first2 = Michael|date= April 19, 2013|  work = The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Boston Marathon bombings meeting in Situation Room.jpg|thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the [[White House Situation Room]] on the morning of April 19]]
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author= |url= http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |work= |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html |title=Bombing manhunt locks down Boston |publisher=CNN |date=September 11, 2012 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times | date = April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web| year = 2013 | month = Apr | url= http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston | first =Adam Clark | last = Estes | publisher = The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded.<ref name=nytdragnet/> One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.<ref name=nytdragnet/>  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/|title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ]]|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and is being treated at [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html|title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect|publisher=''[[The Boston Globe]]''|first1=Kay|last1=Lazar|first2=Martine|last2=Powers|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie | agency = Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 | work =[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news| publisher =CBS | agency = Associated Press | title = 1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url = http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.<ref name="RanOver">{{cite web|url = http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/18/search-for-marathon-bombing-suspect-locks-down-watertown-surrounding-communities/UAbtwLVGLwBE5VI7BUyQuL/story.html|title=Polic comb street of Watertown for Marathon bombing suspect|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion>{{cite news |last1=Ballou |first1=Brian |last2=Wesley  |first2=Lowery |title=Police search Cambridge apartment of suspected bombers: Area near Inman Square blocked off |url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/police-search-apartment-norfolk-street-near-inman-square-cambridge/4OlD6ycJWYPPaZVSQqlqpN/story.html |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion/>

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{Citation | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ | title = Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies | publisher = ABC | newspaper = News | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}.</ref>

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]] and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan Airport]] remains open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The [[National Hockey League]] postponed the playoff implicating game between the [[Boston Bruins]] and [[Pittsburgh Penguins]]<ref>{{Citation | url = http://bruins.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=666714 | title = Bruins | publisher = NHL}}.</ref> after the club with local authorities canceled the "morning skate" practices.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://bruins.nhl.com/club/page.htm?id=60411&navid=DL | publisher = NHL | title = Bruins Blog}}</ref>

[[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=(7) IEDs have been recovered|url=http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/|publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>
MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia.".

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The National Hockey League postponed the playoff implicating game between the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins. after the club with local authorities canceled the "morning skate" practices.

NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the 19-year-old suspect currently at large

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, born in Kyrgyzstan, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident.  

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.wikitext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near Building 32 ([[Stata Center]]) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web|url = http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |publisher=Boston Globe|title= Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1 =Shelley | last1 = Murphy | first2 = Milton J | last2 = Valencia | first3 = Wesley | last3 = Lowery | first4 = Akilah | last4 = Johnson | first5 = Eric | last5 = Moskowitz | first6 = Lisa | last6 = Wangsness | first7 = John R | last7 = Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://emergency.mit.net/emergency | publisher = MIT | title = Emergency Information | date = April 19, 2013}}.</ref> Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven | first = Stephanie|date = April 19, 2013|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url = http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds.<ref name = SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye | first1 = Katherine Q | last2 = Cooper | first2 = Michael|date= April 19, 2013|  work = The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Boston Marathon bombings meeting in Situation Room.jpg|thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the [[White House Situation Room]] on the morning of April 19]]
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached. MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired.. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia.".

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The National Hockey League postponed the playoff implicating game between the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins. after the club with local authorities canceled the "morning skate" practices.

NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the 19-year-old suspect currently at large

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, born in Kyrgyzstan, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident.  

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the 19-year-old suspect currently at large

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, born in Kyrgyzstan, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident.  

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Although the brothers' uncle and aunt insisted that Islam played no role in their actions, several analysts suspect that they were influenced by Islamic jihad (and not the Chechen insurgent cause). The suspects' YouTube, Twitter, and other accounts reportedly have several Islamic references. One suspect reportedly published a video of Osama bin Laden calling on Muslims to kill Americans, Christians, and Jews.[http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/boston-bombing-suspect-liked-terrorism-videos-on-youtube/

Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/|title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ]]|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and is being treated at [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html|title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect|publisher=''[[The Boston Globe]]''|first1=Kay|last1=Lazar|first2=Martine|last2=Powers|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie | agency = Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 | work =[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news| publisher =CBS | agency = Associated Press | title = 1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url = http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.<ref name="RanOver">{{cite web|url = http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/18/search-for-marathon-bombing-suspect-locks-down-watertown-surrounding-communities/UAbtwLVGLwBE5VI7BUyQuL/story.html|title=Polic comb street of Watertown for Marathon bombing suspect|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{Citation | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ | title = Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies | publisher = ABC | newspaper = News | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref>

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The National Hockey League postponed a game between the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins after the club with local authorities canceled the "morning skate" practices.

NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The National Hockey League postponed a game between the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins
NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."

NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The National Hockey League postponed a game between the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins

thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the 19-year-old suspect currently at large

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, born in Kyrgyzstan, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident.  

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Although the brothers' uncle and aunt insisted that Islam played no role in their actions, several analysts suspect that they were influenced by Islamic jihad (and not the Chechen insurgent cause). The suspects' YouTube, Twitter, and other accounts reportedly have several Islamic references. One suspect reportedly published a video of Osama bin Laden calling on Muslims to kill Americans, Christians, and Jews.Official: Boston Bombings Suspect ‘Liked’ Terrorism Videos On YouTube « CBS BostonBoston Marathon suspects Islamic terrorists, not Chechen separatists | Fox NewsBoston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For Bombing

MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."

NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The National Hockey League postponed a game between the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins

It has been reported that after a firefight, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev is "down."

Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."

NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them.<ref name='FBI18AprSuspectPics'>{{cite web |url=http://www.fbi.gov/news/updates-on-investigation-into-multiple-explosions-in-boston/updates-on-investigation-into-multiple-explosions-in-boston |title=Updates on Investigation Into Multiple Explosions in Boston — Video and Photos Released in Bombings Case |accessdate=April 18, 2013 |date=Apr 18, 2013 |work=The FBI Federal Bureau of Investigation |publisher= Department of Justice | place = US}}</ref><ref name="CNN_Smith">{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/18/us/boston-blasts/index.html |title= FBI: Help us ID Boston bomb suspects|last1 = Smith|first1 = Matthew 'Matt' | first2 = Thomas 'Thom' | last2 = Patterson|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded.<ref>{{cite news | title=FBI Releases Images of Two Suspects in Boston Attack|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-set-to-mourn-bombing-victims.html?pagewanted=all|accessdate=April 18, 2013|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=April 18, 2013}}</ref> 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev ([[Chechen language]]: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Джохар Царнаев).<ref name="AtlanticWire04192013">{{cite web | last = Abad-Santos | first = Alexander | title = Who Is Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the Man at the Center of the Boston Manhunt? | publisher = The Atlantic | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/who-is-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-boston/64382/ | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref> Ethnic [[Chechens]] from the North [[Caucasus]], the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.<ref name="NYTimes04192013" /><ref>{{cite news |url=http://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424127887324493704578432030609754740.html |title=Boston Bombing Suspect Killed in Shootout|date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Wall Street Journal |first1=Evan |last1=Perez |first2=Jennifer |last2=Smith |first3=Pervaiz |last3=Shallwani |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html|title=One Boston Bombing Suspect Is Dead, Second at Large; Area on Lockdown|date=April 19, 2013|newspaper=New York Times|author=Katharine Q. run|author=Michael Pearson and Ben Brumfield|date=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CNN}}</ref>  They had been living in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], for the prior ten years.<ref name="AtlanticWire04192013" />  They had previously lived in [[Tokmok]], [[Kyrgyzstan]]<ref name="WashPost04192013">{{cite web | last = Finn | first = Peter | title =  Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal conflict | publisher = Washington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/details-emerge-on-suspected-boston-bombers/2013/04/19/ef2c2566-a8e4-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_story.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref> and [[Makhachkala]], [[Dagestan]], [[Russia]].<ref name="SullivanAP04192013">{{cite news | last = Sullivan | first = Eileen | title =  Manhunt in Boston after bombing suspect is killed | agency = Associated Press | date = April 19, 2013 | url =  http://apnews.myway.com/article/20130419/DA5OPNCO2.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  Both brothers are [[Muslims]].<ref name="HuffPost04192013">{{cite web | last = | title =  Brothers Seen as Good Students and Avid Athletes | publisher = New York Times | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/details-of-tsarnaev-brothers-boston-suspects-emerge.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Boston-Marathon-Bombing-Suspects-JFK-NYC-Travel-International-203787721.html | title = Boston marathon bombing suspects}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Boston manhunt for bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev– live updates|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-mit-police-dead-watertown|accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper= The Guardian | place = UK}}</ref><ref name="AtlanticWire04192013" /><ref name="ForeignPolicy04192013" /> He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."<ref name="AtlanticWire04192013" />  He had been arrested in 2009 for [[domestic assault]] and [[Battery (crime)|battery]], after assaulting his girlfriend.<ref name="ForeignPolicy04192013"> {{cite web | last = Kenner | first = David | title = Who Is Tamerlan Tsarnaev | publisher = Foreign Policy | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://blog.foreignpolicy.com/posts/2013/04/19/who_is_tamerlan_tzarnaev? | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a [[Permanent residence (United States)|permanent resident]].<ref name=CNN130419>{{cite news|title=Bombing manhunt: Where is the suspect hiding?|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html?hpt=hp_t1|accessdate=April 19, 2013|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>  

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the [[University of Massachusetts Dartmouth]], with a major in marine biology.<ref name=guard_tsarnaev>{{cite news|title=Dzhokhar Tsarnaev: Boston bombing suspect was pupil at Cambridge high school|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-suspect-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-school| place = UK | newspaper= The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/news/national/boston-marathon-suspects-tamerlan-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-appeared-lead-normal-lives-article-1.1321715|title=Boston Marathon suspects Tamerlan, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev: Brothers appeared to lead normal lives|newspaper=New York Daily News}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/19/bombing-suspect-attended-umass-dartmouth-prompting-school-closure-college-friend-shocked-charge-boston-marathon-bomber/YcEDA5nvNDi0T1jJTNjKiP/story.html|title=Bombing suspect attended UMass Dartmouth, prompting school closure; college friend shocked by charge he is Boston Marathon bomber|newspaper=boston.com}}</ref>  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.<ref name=CNN130419/>  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Marathon bombers: suspect Dzhozkar Tsarnaev's uncle Ruslan Tsarni pleads 'turn yourself in'|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/northamerica/usa/10006657/Boston-Marathon-bombers-suspect-Dzhozkar-Tsarnaevs-uncle-Ruslan-Tsarni-pleads-turn-yourself-in.html|agency=Associated Press|date=April 19, 2013|work=The Telegraph|publisher=Telegraph Media|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Although the brothers' uncle and aunt insisted that [[Islam]] played no role in their actions, several analysts suspect that they were influenced by Islamic [[jihad]] (and not the Chechen insurgent cause). The suspects' [[YouTube]], [[Twitter]], and other accounts reportedly have several Islamic references. One suspect reportedly published a video of [[Osama bin Laden]] calling on Muslims to kill Americans, Christians, and Jews.<ref>[http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/boston-bombing-suspect-liked-terrorism-videos-on-youtube/ Official: Boston Bombings Suspect ‘Liked’ Terrorism Videos On YouTube « CBS Boston<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[http://www.foxnews.com/opinion/2013/04/19/boston-terror-suspects-islamic-terrorists-not-chechen-separatists/ Boston Marathon suspects Islamic terrorists, not Chechen separatists | Fox News<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/04/19/boston-bombing-suspects-muslim_n_3116299.html Boston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For Bombing<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/details-of-tsarnaev-brothers-boston-suspects-emerge.html?pagewanted=all]</ref>

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev (Chechen language: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident.  

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Although the brothers' uncle and aunt insisted that Islam played no role in their actions, several analysts suspect that they were influenced by Islamic jihad (and not the Chechen insurgent cause). The suspects' YouTube, Twitter, and other accounts reportedly have several Islamic references. One suspect reportedly published a video of Osama bin Laden calling on Muslims to kill Americans, Christians, and Jews.Official: Boston Bombings Suspect ‘Liked’ Terrorism Videos On YouTube « CBS BostonBoston Marathon suspects Islamic terrorists, not Chechen separatists | Fox NewsBoston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For Bombing

[[File:Boston Marathon bombings meeting in Situation Room.jpg|thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the [[White House Situation Room]] on the morning of April 19]]
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author= |url= http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |work= |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]], Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html |title=Bombing manhunt locks down Boston |publisher=CNN |date=September 11, 2012 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times | date = April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web| year = 2013 | month = Apr | url= http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston | first =Adam Clark | last = Estes | publisher = The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded.<ref name=nytdragnet/> One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.<ref name=nytdragnet/>  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/|title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ]]|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and is being treated at [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html|title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect|publisher=''[[The Boston Globe]]''|first1=Kay|last1=Lazar|first2=Martine|last2=Powers|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie | agency = Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 | work =[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news| publisher =CBS | agency = Associated Press | title = 1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url = http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.<ref name="RanOver">{{cite web|url = http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/18/search-for-marathon-bombing-suspect-locks-down-watertown-surrounding-communities/UAbtwLVGLwBE5VI7BUyQuL/story.html|title=Polic comb street of Watertown for Marathon bombing suspect|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion>{{cite news |last1=Ballou |first1=Brian |last2=Wesley  |first2=Lowery |title=Police search Cambridge apartment of suspected bombers: Area near Inman Square blocked off |url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/police-search-apartment-norfolk-street-near-inman-square-cambridge/4OlD6ycJWYPPaZVSQqlqpN/story.html |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion/>

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{Citation | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ | title = Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies | publisher = ABC | newspaper = News | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref>

[[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=(7) IEDs have been recovered|url=http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/|publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]] and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan Airport]] remains open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The [[National Hockey League]] postponed a game between the [[Boston Bruins]] and [[Pittsburgh Penguins]]<ref>{{Citation | url = http://bruins.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=666714 | title = Bruins | publisher = NHL}}</ref>.  Also, [[Major League Baseball]] has postponed a game between the [[Boston Red Sox]] and the [[Kansas City Royals]]<ref>{{Citation | url = http://kansascity.royals.mlb.com/news/print.jsp?ymd=20130419&content_id=45220634&c_id=kc | title = As events unfold, Red Sox game postponed | publisher = MLB}}</ref>.
MIT shooting and Watertown incident.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."

NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The National Hockey League postponed a game between the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins.  Also, Major League Baseball has postponed a game between the Boston Red Sox and the Kansas City Royals.

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Although the brothers' uncle and aunt insisted that Islam played no role in their actions, several analysts suspect that they were influenced by Islamic jihad (and not the Chechen insurgent cause). The suspects' YouTube, Twitter, and other accounts reportedly have several Islamic references. One suspect reportedly published a video of Osama bin Laden calling on Muslims to kill Americans, Christians, and Jews.Official: Boston Bombings Suspect ‘Liked’ Terrorism Videos On YouTube « CBS BostonBoston Marathon suspects Islamic terrorists, not Chechen separatists | Fox NewsBoston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For Bombing

After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19
The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", is "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.

Two law enforcement officials familiar with the case said Tsarnaev ran over his own brother, who had been shot by police, as he fled police in Watertown. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel are taking part in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.

The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."

NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed. The National Hockey League postponed a game between the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins.  Also, Major League Baseball has postponed a game between the Boston Red Sox and the Kansas City Royals.

On the evening of April 19, the second suspect was surrounded in a boat in the yard of a home in Watertown.
