In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:45 PM ET after a standoff,<ref>{{cite web|title=Bombing suspect surrounded in Watertown|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/breakingnews/ci_23065406/sun-staff-and-news-services|publisher=The Lowell Sun|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Shots Fired In Watertown (UPDATE: Police Have Suspect In Custody)|url=http://www.mediaite.com/online/breaking-shots-fired-in-watertown/|publisher=Mediaite|accessdate=20 April 2013}}</ref> and taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]]. Before he was taken into custody, police used ''flash bang'' stun grenades to disorient and distract him.
MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through thermal imaging cameras. It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered. Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.https://twitter.com/Boston_Police/status/325409894830329856

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:45 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital. Before he was taken into custody, police used flash bang stun grenades to disorient and distract him.

thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. The brothers' uncle and aunt insisted that the religion  played no role in their motivation for the bombing.Boston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For BombingBrothers Seen as Good Students and Avid Athletes

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev was found and taken into federal custody after a standoff on April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved 20 April 2013.

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev was found and taken into federal custody after a standoff on April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved 20 April 2013.

[[File:Boston Marathon bombings meeting in Situation Room.jpg|thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the [[White House Situation Room]] on the morning of April 19]]

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author= |url= http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |work= |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]], Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html |title=Bombing manhunt locks down Boston |publisher=CNN |date=September 11, 2012 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times | date = April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web| year = 2013 | month = Apr | url= http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston | first =Adam Clark | last = Estes | publisher = The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded.<ref name=nytdragnet/> One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.<ref name=nytdragnet/>  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/|title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ]]|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and is being treated at [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html|title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect|publisher=''[[The Boston Globe]]''|first1=Kay|last1=Lazar|first2=Martine|last2=Powers|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie | agency = Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 | work =[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news| publisher =CBS | agency = Associated Press | title = 1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url = http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.<ref name="RanOver">{{cite web|url = http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/18/search-for-marathon-bombing-suspect-locks-down-watertown-surrounding-communities/UAbtwLVGLwBE5VI7BUyQuL/story.html|title=Polic comb street of Watertown for Marathon bombing suspect|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion>{{cite news |last1=Ballou |first1=Brian |last2=Wesley  |first2=Lowery |title=Police search Cambridge apartment of suspected bombers: Area near Inman Square blocked off |url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/police-search-apartment-norfolk-street-near-inman-square-cambridge/4OlD6ycJWYPPaZVSQqlqpN/story.html |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion/> The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{Citation | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ | title = Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies | publisher = ABC | newspaper = News | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref> [[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=(7) IEDs have been recovered|url=http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/|publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through [[thermal imaging]] cameras.<ref>https://twitter.com/NBCNewsUS/status/325398581097947136</ref> It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.<ref>http://tv.msnbc.com/2013/04/19/shots-fired-in-watertown/</ref><ref>http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-its-over-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive-police-say</ref><ref>http://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2013/04/19/boston-marathon-explosions-live-updates-3/?hpid=z2#liveblog-entry-13798</ref> Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.<ref>https://twitter.com/Boston_Police/status/325409894830329856</ref>

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]] and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan Airport]] remains open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:45 PM ET after a standoff,<ref>{{cite web|title=Bombing suspect surrounded in Watertown|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/breakingnews/ci_23065406/sun-staff-and-news-services|publisher=The Lowell Sun|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Shots Fired In Watertown (UPDATE: Police Have Suspect In Custody)|url=http://www.mediaite.com/online/breaking-shots-fired-in-watertown/|publisher=Mediaite|accessdate=20 April 2013}}</ref> and taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]]. Before he was taken into custody, police used ''flash bang'' stun grenades to disorient and distract him.
MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through thermal imaging cameras.https://twitter.com/NBCNewsUS/status/325398581097947136 It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.http://tv.msnbc.com/2013/04/19/shots-fired-in-watertown/http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-its-over-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive-police-sayhttp://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2013/04/19/boston-marathon-explosions-live-updates-3/?hpid=z2#liveblog-entry-13798 Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.https://twitter.com/Boston_Police/status/325409894830329856

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:45 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital. Before he was taken into custody, police used flash bang stun grenades to disorient and distract him.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:45 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital. Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved 20 April 2013.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through thermal imaging cameras.https://twitter.com/NBCNewsUS/status/325398581097947136 It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.http://tv.msnbc.com/2013/04/19/shots-fired-in-watertown/http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-its-over-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive-police-sayhttp://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2013/04/19/boston-marathon-explosions-live-updates-3/?hpid=z2#liveblog-entry-13798 Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.https://twitter.com/Boston_Police/status/325409894830329856

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:45 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used flash bang stun grenades to disorient and distract him.

thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos about terrorism, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved 20 April 2013.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.wikitext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near Building 32 ([[Stata Center]]) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web|url = http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |publisher=Boston Globe|title= Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1 =Shelley | last1 = Murphy | first2 = Milton J | last2 = Valencia | first3 = Wesley | last3 = Lowery | first4 = Akilah | last4 = Johnson | first5 = Eric | last5 = Moskowitz | first6 = Lisa | last6 = Wangsness | first7 = John R | last7 = Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://emergency.mit.net/emergency | publisher = MIT | title = Emergency Information | date = April 19, 2013}}</ref> Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven | first = Stephanie|date = April 19, 2013|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url = http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds.<ref name = SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye | first1 = Katherine Q | last2 = Cooper | first2 = Michael|date= April 19, 2013|  work = The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Boston Marathon bombings meeting in Situation Room.jpg|thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the [[White House Situation Room]] on the morning of April 19]]

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author= |url= http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |work= |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]], Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html |title=Bombing manhunt locks down Boston |publisher=CNN |date=September 11, 2012 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times | date = April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web| year = 2013 | month = Apr | url= http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston | first =Adam Clark | last = Estes | publisher = The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded.<ref name=nytdragnet/> One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.<ref name=nytdragnet/>  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/|title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ]]|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and is being treated at [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html|title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect|publisher=''[[The Boston Globe]]''|first1=Kay|last1=Lazar|first2=Martine|last2=Powers|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie | agency = Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 | work =[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news| publisher =CBS | agency = Associated Press | title = 1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url = http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.<ref name="RanOver">{{cite web|url = http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/18/search-for-marathon-bombing-suspect-locks-down-watertown-surrounding-communities/UAbtwLVGLwBE5VI7BUyQuL/story.html|title=Polic comb street of Watertown for Marathon bombing suspect|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion>{{cite news |last1=Ballou |first1=Brian |last2=Wesley  |first2=Lowery |title=Police search Cambridge apartment of suspected bombers: Area near Inman Square blocked off |url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/police-search-apartment-norfolk-street-near-inman-square-cambridge/4OlD6ycJWYPPaZVSQqlqpN/story.html |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion/> The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{Citation | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ | title = Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies | publisher = ABC | newspaper = News | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref> [[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=(7) IEDs have been recovered|url=http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/|publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through [[thermal imaging]] cameras.<ref>https://twitter.com/NBCNewsUS/status/325398581097947136</ref> It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.<ref>http://tv.msnbc.com/2013/04/19/shots-fired-in-watertown/</ref><ref>http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-its-over-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive-police-say</ref><ref>http://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2013/04/19/boston-marathon-explosions-live-updates-3/?hpid=z2#liveblog-entry-13798</ref> Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.<ref>https://twitter.com/Boston_Police/status/325409894830329856</ref>

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]] and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan Airport]] remains open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff,<ref>{{cite web|title=Bombing suspect surrounded in Watertown|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/breakingnews/ci_23065406/sun-staff-and-news-services|publisher=The Lowell Sun|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Shots Fired In Watertown (UPDATE: Police Have Suspect In Custody)|url=http://www.mediaite.com/online/breaking-shots-fired-in-watertown/|publisher=Mediaite|accessdate=20 April 2013}}</ref> and taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]] in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used ''flash bang'' stun grenades to disorient and distract him.
MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through thermal imaging cameras.https://twitter.com/NBCNewsUS/status/325398581097947136 It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.http://tv.msnbc.com/2013/04/19/shots-fired-in-watertown/http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-its-over-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive-police-sayhttp://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2013/04/19/boston-marathon-explosions-live-updates-3/?hpid=z2#liveblog-entry-13798 Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.https://twitter.com/Boston_Police/status/325409894830329856

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used flash bang stun grenades to disorient and distract him.

thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos about terrorism, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved 20 April 2013.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.wikitext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near Building 32 ([[Stata Center]]) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web|url = http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |publisher=Boston Globe|title= Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1 =Shelley | last1 = Murphy | first2 = Milton J | last2 = Valencia | first3 = Wesley | last3 = Lowery | first4 = Akilah | last4 = Johnson | first5 = Eric | last5 = Moskowitz | first6 = Lisa | last6 = Wangsness | first7 = John R | last7 = Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://emergency.mit.net/emergency | publisher = MIT | title = Emergency Information | date = April 19, 2013}}</ref> Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven | first = Stephanie|date = April 19, 2013|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url = http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds.<ref name = SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye | first1 = Katherine Q | last2 = Cooper | first2 = Michael|date= April 19, 2013|  work = The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Boston Marathon bombings meeting in Situation Room.jpg|thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the [[White House Situation Room]] on the morning of April 19]]

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author= |url= http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |work= |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]], Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html |title=Bombing manhunt locks down Boston |publisher=CNN |date=September 11, 2012 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times | date = April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web| year = 2013 | month = Apr | url= http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston | first =Adam Clark | last = Estes | publisher = The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded.<ref name=nytdragnet/> One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.<ref name=nytdragnet/>  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/|title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ]]|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and is being treated at [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html|title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect|publisher=''[[The Boston Globe]]''|first1=Kay|last1=Lazar|first2=Martine|last2=Powers|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan |first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie | agency = Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 | work =[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news| publisher =CBS | agency = Associated Press | title = 1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials.<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url = http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.<ref name="RanOver">{{cite web|url = http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/18/search-for-marathon-bombing-suspect-locks-down-watertown-surrounding-communities/UAbtwLVGLwBE5VI7BUyQuL/story.html|title=Polic comb street of Watertown for Marathon bombing suspect|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion>{{cite news |last1=Ballou |first1=Brian |last2=Wesley  |first2=Lowery |title=Police search Cambridge apartment of suspected bombers: Area near Inman Square blocked off |url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/police-search-apartment-norfolk-street-near-inman-square-cambridge/4OlD6ycJWYPPaZVSQqlqpN/story.html |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it.<ref name=BG-controlled-explosion/> The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{Citation | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ | title = Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies | publisher = ABC | newspaper = News | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref> [[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=(7) IEDs have been recovered|url=http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/|publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through [[thermal imaging]] cameras.<ref>https://twitter.com/NBCNewsUS/status/325398581097947136</ref> It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.<ref>http://tv.msnbc.com/2013/04/19/shots-fired-in-watertown/</ref><ref>http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-its-over-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive-police-say</ref><ref>http://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2013/04/19/boston-marathon-explosions-live-updates-3/?hpid=z2#liveblog-entry-13798</ref> Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.<ref>https://twitter.com/Boston_Police/status/325409894830329856</ref>

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]] and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan Airport]] remains open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff,<ref>{{cite web|title=Bombing suspect surrounded in Watertown|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/breakingnews/ci_23065406/sun-staff-and-news-services|publisher=The Lowell Sun|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Shots Fired In Watertown (UPDATE: Police Have Suspect In Custody)|url=http://www.mediaite.com/online/breaking-shots-fired-in-watertown/|publisher=Mediaite|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> and taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]] in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used ''flash bang'' stun grenades to disorient and distract him.

Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through thermal imaging cameras.https://twitter.com/NBCNewsUS/status/325398581097947136 It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.http://tv.msnbc.com/2013/04/19/shots-fired-in-watertown/http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-its-over-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive-police-sayhttp://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2013/04/19/boston-marathon-explosions-live-updates-3/?hpid=z2#liveblog-entry-13798 Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.https://twitter.com/Boston_Police/status/325409894830329856

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used flash bang stun grenades to disorient and distract him.

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos about terrorism, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved April 20, 2013.

The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan Airport]] remains open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff,<ref>{{cite web|title=Bombing suspect surrounded in Watertown|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/breakingnews/ci_23065406/sun-staff-and-news-services|publisher=The Lowell Sun|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Shots Fired In Watertown (UPDATE: Police Have Suspect In Custody)|url=http://www.mediaite.com/online/breaking-shots-fired-in-watertown/|publisher=Mediaite|accessdate=20 April 2013}}</ref> and taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]] in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used ''flash bang'' stun grenades to disorient and distract him.
MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through thermal imaging cameras.https://twitter.com/NBCNewsUS/status/325398581097947136 It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.http://tv.msnbc.com/2013/04/19/shots-fired-in-watertown/http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-its-over-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive-police-sayhttp://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2013/04/19/boston-marathon-explosions-live-updates-3/?hpid=z2#liveblog-entry-13798 Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.https://twitter.com/Boston_Police/status/325409894830329856

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used flash bang stun grenades to disorient and distract him.
