thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos about terrorism, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved 20 April 2013.

thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos about terrorism, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.   He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved 20 April 2013.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. Tsarnaev Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used flash bang stun grenades to disorient and distract him.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two videos about terrorism, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. 

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.   He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved 20 April 2013.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through thermal imaging cameras.Twitter / NBCNewsUS: UPDATE: Police responded to It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.Boston bombing suspect in custody — MSNBCIt's over: Boston bombing suspect captured alive, police say - U.S. NewsBoston bombing manhunt: Live updates as police look for Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. Tsarnaev Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff.

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two immigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two radical Islamist videos, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. He told a photographer: ""God said no alcohol. There are no values anymore… people can't control themselves."  

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.   He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. It concluded with Tsarnaev hiding in a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered through thermal imaging cameras.Twitter / NBCNewsUS: UPDATE: Police responded to It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.Boston bombing suspect in custody — MSNBCIt's over: Boston bombing suspect captured alive, police say - U.S. NewsBoston bombing manhunt: Live updates as police look for Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

In the evening of April 19, authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge hiding under the canvas of a boat in the backyard of a property in Watertown. He was taken into federal custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two radical Islamist videos, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. He told a photographer: ""God said no alcohol. There are no values anymore… people can't control themselves."  

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.   He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved 20 April 2013.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two radical Islamist videos, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. He told a photographer: ""God said no alcohol. There are no values anymore… people can't control themselves."  

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.   He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved April 20, 2013.

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. A YouTube account in Tamerlan's name featured two radical Islamist videos, and Tamerlan's aunt said that in recent years, he had become increasingly observant and began praying five times a day. He told a photographer: "God said no alcohol. There are no values anymore… people can't control themselves."  

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.   He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved April 20, 2013.

After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. Authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge under a canvas of a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered by the boat's owner David Henneberry, and verified through thermal imaging cameras.Twitter / NBCNewsUS: UPDATE: Police responded to It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.Boston bombing suspect in custody — MSNBCIt's over: Boston bombing suspect captured alive, police say - U.S. NewsBoston bombing manhunt: Live updates as police look for Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance. Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. He told a photographer: "God said no alcohol. There are no values anymore… people can't control themselves."  

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.   He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved April 20, 2013.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. Authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge under a canvas of a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered by the boat's owner David Henneberry, and later verified through thermal imaging cameras.Twitter / NBCNewsUS: UPDATE: Police responded to It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.Boston bombing suspect in custody — MSNBCIt's over: Boston bombing suspect captured alive, police say - U.S. NewsBoston bombing manhunt: Live updates as police look for Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.. He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used flash bang stun grenades to disorient and distract him.

MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. Authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge under a canvas of a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered by the boat's owner David Henneberry, and later verified through thermal imaging cameras.Twitter / NBCNewsUS: UPDATE: Police responded to It has been reported that the boat was on fire after he had been cornered.Boston bombing suspect in custody — MSNBCIt's over: Boston bombing suspect captured alive, police say - U.S. NewsBoston bombing manhunt: Live updates as police look for Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.Twitter / Boston_Police: Suspect in custody. Officers He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance. Before he was taken into custody, police used flash bang stun grenades to disorient and distract him.

After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

Officers He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance. Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

In a 5:20 p.m. news conference on April 18, the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. According to the FBI, one of the suspects was seen placing a backpack at the scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. 

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims. He told a photographer: "God said no alcohol. There are no values anymore… people can't control themselves."  

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery, after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He was born in Russia. 

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive – live updates - The Guardian. Retrieved April 20, 2013.

After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near Building 32 ([[Stata Center]]) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web|url = http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |publisher=Boston Globe|title= Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1 =Shelley | last1 = Murphy | first2 = Milton J | last2 = Valencia | first3 = Wesley | last3 = Lowery | first4 = Akilah | last4 = Johnson | first5 = Eric | last5 = Moskowitz | first6 = Lisa | last6 = Wangsness | first7 = John R | last7 = Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref> Multiple shots were fired.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://emergency.mit.net/emergency | publisher = MIT | title = Emergency Information | date = April 19, 2013}}</ref> Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven | first = Stephanie|date = April 19, 2013|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url = http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds.<ref name = SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye | first1 = Katherine Q | last2 = Cooper | first2 = Michael|date= April 19, 2013|  work = The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Boston Marathon bombings meeting in Situation Room.jpg|thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the [[White House Situation Room]] on the morning of April 19]]

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.{{cn}} They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author= |url= http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |work= |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]], Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/index.html |title=Bombing manhunt locks down Boston |publisher=CNN |date=September 11, 2012 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times | date = April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web| year = 2013 | month = Apr | url= http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston | first =Adam Clark | last = Estes | publisher = The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded.<ref name=nytdragnet/> One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.<ref name=nytdragnet/>  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. MIT shooting and Watertown incidents.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. Authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge under a canvas of a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered by the boat's owner David Henneberry, and later verified through thermal imaging cameras.Twitter / NBCNewsUS: UPDATE: Police responded to Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.Twitter / Boston_Police: Suspect in custody. Officers He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near Building 32 (Stata Center) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. Authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge under a canvas of a Watertown resident's boat, which was discovered by the boat's owner David Henneberry, and later verified through thermal imaging cameras.Twitter / NBCNewsUS: UPDATE: Police responded to Boston Police Department stated that Tsarnaev had been arrested.Twitter / Boston_Police: Suspect in custody. Officers He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance.

After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel partook in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. According to one of the officials' news conferences on the morning of April 19, the police will conduct a controlled explosion at the house that afternoon.  Authorities did not provide details on the nature of the controlled explosion or the reason for it. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. Authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After their photos were released, a shooting followed on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Multiple{[quantify}} shots were fired. Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

thumb|left|President Obama meeting with advisers in the White House Situation Room on the morning of April 19

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect was captured; the other managed to escape in the SUV.  A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and is being treated at Mount Auburn Hospital, where he is described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, one suspect, Tamerlan Tsarnaev, was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large", according to law enforcement officials. The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge, authorities said.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far, some in Watertown, some at the house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most of Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remains open. Universities, schools, businesses and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19. Authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev as he took refuge under a canvas of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, he saw blood on the tarp of the boat. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras.Twitter / NBCNewsUS: UPDATE: Police responded to Boston Police Department tweeted that Tsarnaev had been arrested.Twitter / Boston_Police: Suspect in custody. Officers He was taken into custody around 8:42 PM ET after a standoff, and taken to Mount Auburn Hospital in an ambulance.
