On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, claimed he providing detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him 2 1/2 minutes before the blast.http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the prior ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in Russia.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, living in Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19..

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects fired multiple shots at a policeman on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car, received multiple gunshot wounds. Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. The two suspects exchanged gunfire with police and threw a pressure cooker bomb at them, which exploded in midair after the lid failed. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".  Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. The two suspects exchanged gunfire with police and threw a pressure cooker bomb at them, which exploded in midair after the lid failed. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the canvas cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose and the lines securing the tarp had been cut, lifted the tarp to investigate, and saw a human form lying in a pool of blood. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was in serious condition..

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them.<ref name='FBI18AprSuspectPics'>{{cite web |url= http://www.fbi.gov/news/updates-on-investigation-into-multiple-explosions-in-boston/updates-on-investigation-into-multiple-explosions-in-boston |title=Updates on Investigation Into Multiple Explosions in Boston — Video and Photos Released in Bombings Case |accessdate=April 18, 2013 |date=Apr 18, 2013 |work=The FBI Federal Bureau of Investigation |publisher= Department of Justice | place = US}}</ref><ref name="CNN_Smith">{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/18/us/boston-blasts/index.html |title= FBI: Help us ID Boston bomb suspects|last1 = Smith|first1 = Matthew 'Matt' | first2 = Thomas 'Thom' | last2 = Patterson|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded.<ref>{{cite news | title=FBI Releases Images of Two Suspects in Boston Attack|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-set-to-mourn-bombing-victims.html?pagewanted=all|accessdate=April 18, 2013|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=April 18, 2013}}</ref> Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, claimed he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him 2 1/2 minutes before the blast.<ref>http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/</ref>

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev.<ref name="AtlanticWire04192013">{{cite web | last = Abad-Santos | first = Alexander | title = Who Is Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the Man at the Center of the Boston Manhunt? | publisher = The Atlantic | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/who-is-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-boston/64382/ | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref> Ethnic [[Chechens]] from the [[North Caucasus]], the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.<ref name="NYTimes04192013" /><ref>{{cite news |url=http://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424127887324493704578432030609754740.html |title=Boston Bombing Suspect Killed in Shootout|date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Wall Street Journal |first1=Evan |last1=Perez |first2=Jennifer |last2=Smith |first3=Pervaiz |last3=Shallwani |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html|title=One Boston Bombing Suspect Is Dead, Second at Large; Area on Lockdown|date=April 19, 2013|newspaper= The New York Times| first1 =Katharine Q | last1 = Seelye | first2 = Michael | last2 = Cooper}}</ref><ref name="captured">{{cite news|url= http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/ |title= 'Captured!!!' living in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], for the prior ten years.<ref name = "AtlanticWire04192013" />  They had previously lived in [[Tokmok]], [[Kyrgyzstan]], and [[Makhachkala]], [[Dagestan]], [[Russia]].<ref name="WashPost04192013">{{cite web | last = Finn | first = Peter | title =  Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal conflict | publisher = Washington Post | }}</ref><ref name="SullivanAP04192013">{{cite news | last = Sullivan | first = Eileen | title =  Manhunt in Boston after bombing suspect is killed | agency = Associated Press | date = April 19, 2013 | url =  http://apnews.myway.com/article/20130419/DA5OPNCO2.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  Both brothers are [[Muslims]].<ref name="HuffPost04192013">{{cite web | last = Kaleem | first = Jaweed | title = Boston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For Bombing  | publisher = Huffington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/04/19/boston-bombing-suspects-muslim_n_3116299.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="HuffPostNoronha04192013">{{cite web | last = Noronha | first = college friend shocked by charge he is Boston Marathon bomber|newspaper=boston.com}}</ref>  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.<ref name="WPostGowen04192013" />  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.<ref name="captured" />  On television, his uncle, living in [[Maryland]], pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Marathon bombers: suspect Dzhozkar Tsarnaev's uncle Ruslan Tsarni pleads 'turn yourself in'|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/northamerica/usa/10006657/Boston-Marathon-bombers-suspect-Dzhozkar-Tsarnaevs-uncle-Ruslan-Tsarni-pleads-turn-yourself-in.html| place = UK | agency=Associated Press|date=April 19, 2013|work=The Telegraph|publisher=Telegraph Media|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.<ref name=autogenerated2>{{cite web|title=Bombing suspect surrounded in Watertown|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/breakingnews/ci_23065406/sun-staff-and-news-services|publisher=The Lowell Sun|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web|title=Shots Fired In Watertown (Update: Police Have Suspect In Custody)|url=http://www.mediaite.com/online/breaking-shots-fired-in-watertown/|publisher= Mediaite|accessdate= April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-mit-police-dead-watertown | title = Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive | type = live updates | newspaper = The Guardian | accessdate = April 20, 2013 | year = 2013 | month = Apr}}.</ref>

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".  Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. The two suspects exchanged gunfire with police and threw a pressure cooker bomb at them, which exploded in midair after the lid failed. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the canvas cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was in serious condition..

Suspects.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, claimed he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him 2 1/2 minutes before the blast.http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in Russia.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, living in Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19..

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, claimed he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him 2 1/2 minutes before the blast.http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in Russia.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19..

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".  Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. The two suspects exchanged gunfire with police and threw a pressure cooker bomb at them, which exploded in midair after the lid failed. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was in serious condition..

thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, claimed he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him 2 1/2 minutes before the blast.http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev. Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in Russia.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19..

Manhunt and capture.wikitext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven | first = Stephanie|date = April 19, 2013|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url =http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near the [[Stata Center]] (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web| url = http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |publisher=Boston Globe|title= Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1 =Shelley | last1 = Murphy | first2 = Milton J |last2 = Valencia | first3 = Wesley | last3 = Lowery | first4 = Akilah | last4 = Johnson | first5 = Eric | last5 = Moskowitz | first6 = Lisa | last6 = Wangsness | first7 = John R | last7 = Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref><ref>{{Citation | url = http://emergency.mit.net/emergency | publisher = MIT | title = Emergency Information | date = April 19, 2013}}</ref> <ref name = SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye | first1 = Katherine Q | last2 = Cooper | first2 = Michael|date= April 19, 2013|  work = The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.{{cn}} They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|author= |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |work= |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]], Massachusetts.<ref name="captured" /> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times | date = April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web| year = 2013 | month = Apr | url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston | first =Adam Clark | last = Estes | publisher = The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> The two suspects exchanged gunfire with police and threw a [[pressure cooker bomb]] at them, which exploded in midair after the lid failed.{{cn}} One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-22212946|title=Boston Marathon bomb suspect still at large|publisher=''[[BBC]]''|date=April 20, 2013|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, an MIT police officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".  Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. The two suspects exchanged gunfire with police and threw a pressure cooker bomb at them, which exploded in midair after the lid failed. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was in serious condition..

thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him 2 1/2 minutes before the blast.http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in Russia.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19..

massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", was "still at large".<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url =http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge.<ref name="RanOver">{{cite web|url =http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/18/search-for-marathon-bombing-suspect-locks-down-watertown-surrounding-communities/UAbtwLVGLwBE5VI7BUyQuL/story.html|title=Polic comb street of Watertown for Marathon bombing suspect|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Early on April 19, Watertown residents received [[reverse 911]] calls asking them to stay indoors.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/watertown/2013/04/officials_in_watertown_field_c.html | year = 2013 | month = Apr | title = Officials in Watertown field calls from worried residents – Watertown – Your Town | newspaper = Boston}}.</ref>

You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{Citation | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ | title = Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies | publisher = ABC | newspaper = News | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref> [[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=(7) IEDs have been recovered|url=http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/|publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]], and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan International Airport]] remained open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry,<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Bomb Suspect Captured Alive in Backyard Boat|url=http://abcnews.go.com/US/one-boston-marathon-suspect-dead-second-run-police-say/story?id=18994511|author=Thomas, Pierre; Ross, Brian; Ferran, Lee; Curry, Colleen|date=April 19, 2013|work=ABC News|publisher=|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St.<ref>{{cite news|title=Second Boston Marathon bombing suspect in custody|url=http://www.wcvb.com/Second-Boston-Marathon-bombing-suspect-in-custody/-/9849586/19814816/-/cw8b4az/-/index.html|author=|date=April 20, 2013|work=WCBV.com|publisher=|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police.<ref>{{cite news|title=Watertown family finds alleged marathon bomber in boat|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/watertown-family-finds-alleged-marathon-bomber-boat/y3te9bJyaatLpd4yvLGRGJ/story.html|author=Anderson, Derek J.|date=April 19, 2013|work=Boston Globe|publisher=|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through [[thermal imaging]] cameras.<ref name="captured" /> He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff,<ref name=autogenerated2 /><ref name=autogenerated1 /> and transported to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]] where he was in serious condition.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-we-got-him-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive | title = 'We got him!': Boston bombing suspect captured alive | place = US | newspaper = News | publisher = NBC | date = 2013‐4‐19}}.</ref>
Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".  Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. The two suspects exchanged gunfire with police and threw a pressure cooker bomb at them, which exploded in midair after the lid failed. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended in the evening of April 19 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was in serious condition..

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev ([[Cyrillic script]]: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).<ref name="AtlanticWire04192013">{{cite web | last = Abad-Santos | first = Alexander | title = Who Is Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the Man at the Center of the Boston Manhunt? | publisher = The Atlantic | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/who-is-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-boston/64382/ | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref> Ethnic [[Chechens]] from the [[North Caucasus]], the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.<ref name="NYTimes04192013" /><ref>{{cite news |url=http://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424127887324493704578432030609754740.html |title=Boston Bombing Suspect Killed in Shootout|date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Wall Street Journal |first1=Evan |last1=Perez |first2=Jennifer |last2=Smith |first3=Pervaiz |last3=Shallwani |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html|title=One Boston Bombing Suspect Is Dead, Second at Large; Area on Lockdown|date=April 19, 2013|newspaper= The New York Times| first1 =Katharine Q | last1 = Seelye | first2 = Michael | last2 = Cooper}}</ref><ref name="captured">{{cite news|url= http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/ |title= 'Captured!!!' Boston police announce Marathon bombing suspect in custody| first1 = Chelsea J | last1 = Carter | first2 = Gregory ‘Greg’ | last2 = Botelho|date=April 20, 2013|work= [[CNN]]}}</ref>  They had been living in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], for the past ten years.<ref name = "AtlanticWire04192013" />  They had previously lived in [[Tokmok]], [[Kyrgyzstan]], and [[Makhachkala]], [[Dagestan]], [[Russia]].<ref name="WashPost04192013">{{cite web | last = Finn | first = Peter | title =  Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal conflict | publisher = Washington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/details-emerge-on-suspected-boston-bombers/2013/04/19/ef2c2566-a8e4-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_story.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="SullivanAP04192013">{{cite news | last = Sullivan | first = Eileen | title =  Manhunt in Boston after bombing suspect is killed | agency = Associated Press | date = April 19, 2013 | url =  http://apnews.myway.com/article/20130419/DA5OPNCO2.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  Both brothers are [[Muslims]].<ref name="HuffPost04192013">{{cite web | last = Kaleem | first = Jaweed | title = Boston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For Bombing  | publisher = Huffington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/04/19/boston-bombing-suspects-muslim_n_3116299.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="HuffPostNoronha04192013">{{cite web | last = Noronha | first = http://www.huffingtonpost.com/huff-wires/20130419/cn-canada-boston-marathon-suspects-aunt/# | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="NYTimes04192013">{{cite news | last = Goode | first = Erica | title =  Brothers Seen as Good Students and Avid Athletes | publisher = New York Times | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/details-of-tsarnaev-brothers-boston-suspects-emerge.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>

[[Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Boston Marathon bombings)|Tamerlan Tsarnaev]] (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.<ref>{{Citation | newspaper = News | publisher = NBC | place = New York | url = http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Boston-Marathon-Bombing-Suspects-JFK-NYC-Travel-International-203787721.html | title = Boston marathon bombing suspects}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title =Boston manhunt for bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev– live updates|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-mit-police-dead-watertown|accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper= The Guardian | place = UK}}</ref><ref name="AtlanticWire04192013" /><ref name="ForeignPolicy04192013" />  He was born in Russia.<ref name="WPostGowen04192013">{{Citation | last = Gowen | first = Annie | last2 = Horwitz | first2 = Sari | last3 = Markon | first3 = Jerry | title = Boston lockdown lifted; marathon bombing suspect still at large | newspaper = [[Washington Post]] | year = 2013 | date = April 19 | url = http://www.washingtonpost.com/world/national-security/massive-police-operation-under-way-in-boston/2013/04/19/979ec6dc-a8c6-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_print.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  He had been arrested in 2009 for [[domestic assault]] and [[Battery (crime)|battery]] after assaulting his girlfriend.<ref name="ForeignPolicy04192013"> {{cite web | last = Kenner | first = David | title = Who Is Tamerlan Tsarnaev | publisher = Foreign Policy | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://blog.foreignpolicy.com/posts/2013/04/19/who_is_tamerlan_tzarnaev? | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a [[Permanent residence (United States)|permanent resident]].<ref name="captured" /> He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."<ref name="AtlanticWire04192013" />

college friend shocked by charge he is Boston Marathon bomber|newspaper=boston.com}}</ref>  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.<ref name="WPostGowen04192013" />  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.<ref name="captured" />  On television, his uncle, living in [[Montgomery Village, Maryland]], pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Marathon bombers: suspect Dzhozkar Tsarnaev's uncle Ruslan Tsarni pleads 'turn yourself in'|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/northamerica/usa/10006657/Boston-Marathon-bombers-suspect-Dzhozkar-Tsarnaevs-uncle-Ruslan-Tsarni-pleads-turn-yourself-in.html| place = UK | agency=Associated Press|date=April 19, 2013|work=The Telegraph|publisher=Telegraph Media|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of April 19.<ref name=autogenerated2>{{cite web|title=Bombing suspect surrounded in Watertown|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/breakingnews/ci_23065406/sun-staff-and-news-services|publisher=The Lowell Sun|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web|title=Shots Fired In Watertown (Update: Police Have Suspect In Custody)|url=http://www.mediaite.com/online/breaking-shots-fired-in-watertown/|publisher= Mediaite|accessdate= April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-mit-police-dead-watertown | title = Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive | type = live updates | newspaper = The Guardian | accessdate = April 20, 2013 | year = 2013 | month = Apr}}.</ref>

Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/|title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ]]|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and was taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html|title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect|publisher=''[[The Boston Globe]]''|first1=Kay|last1=Lazar|first2=Martine|last2=Powers|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan|first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie | agency = Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 | work =[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news| publisher =CBS | agency = Associated Press | title = 1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", was "still at large".<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url =http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge.<ref name="RanOver">{{cite web|url =http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/18/search-for-marathon-bombing-suspect-locks-down-watertown-surrounding-communities/UAbtwLVGLwBE5VI7BUyQuL/story.html|title=Polic comb street of Watertown for Marathon bombing suspect|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Early on April 19, Watertown residents received [[reverse 911]] calls asking them to stay indoors.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/watertown/2013/04/officials_in_watertown_field_c.html | year = 2013 | month = Apr | title = Officials in Watertown field calls from worried residents – Watertown – Your Town | newspaper = Boston}}.</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in [[Dagestan]], encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]], and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan International Airport]] remained open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry,<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Bomb Suspect Captured Alive in Backyard Boat|url=http://abcnews.go.com/US/one-boston-marathon-suspect-dead-second-run-police-say/story?id=18994511|author=Thomas, Pierre; Ross, Brian; Ferran, Lee; Curry, Colleen|date=April 19, 2013|work=ABC News|publisher=|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St.<ref>{{cite news|title=Second Boston Marathon bombing suspect in custody|url=http://www.wcvb.com/Second-Boston-Marathon-bombing-suspect-in-custody/-/9849586/19814816/-/cw8b4az/-/index.html|author=|date=April 20, 2013|work=WCBV.com|publisher=|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police.<ref>{{cite news|title=Watertown family finds alleged marathon bomber in boat|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/watertown-family-finds-alleged-marathon-bomber-boat/y3te9bJyaatLpd4yvLGRGJ/story.html|author=Anderson, Derek J.|date=April 19, 2013|work=Boston Globe|publisher=|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through [[thermal imaging]] cameras.<ref name="captured" /> He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff,<ref name=autogenerated2 /><ref name=autogenerated1 /> and transported to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]] where he was in serious condition.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-we-got-him-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive | title = 'We got him!': Boston bombing suspect captured alive | place = US | newspaper = News | publisher = NBC | date = 2013‐4‐19}}.</ref>
Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
thumb|right|150px|upright|Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the younger of the two brothers
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".  Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. The two suspects exchanged gunfire with police and threw a pressure cooker bomb at them, which exploded in midair after the lid failed. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". The brothers had tossed pipe bombs from their car at officers who pursued them into Watertown from Cambridge. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was in serious condition..

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them.<ref name='FBI18AprSuspectPics'>{{cite web |url= http://www.fbi.gov/news/updates-on-investigation-into-multiple-explosions-in-boston/updates-on-investigation-into-multiple-explosions-in-boston |title=Updates on Investigation Into Multiple Explosions in Boston — Video and Photos Released in Bombings Case |accessdate=April 18, 2013 |date=Apr 18, 2013 |work=The FBI Federal Bureau of Investigation |publisher= Department of Justice | place = US}}</ref><ref name="CNN_Smith">{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/18/us/boston-blasts/index.html |title= FBI: Help us ID Boston bomb suspects|last1 = Smith|first1 = Matthew 'Matt' | first2 = Thomas 'Thom' | last2 = Patterson|date=April 19, 2013|work=[[CNN]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded.<ref>{{cite news | title=FBI Releases Images of Two Suspects in Boston Attack|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-set-to-mourn-bombing-victims.html?pagewanted=all|accessdate=April 18, 2013|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=April 18, 2013}}</ref> Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.<ref>http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/</ref>

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev ([[Cyrillic script]]: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).<ref name="AtlanticWire04192013">{{cite web | last = Abad-Santos | first = Alexander | title = Who Is Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the Man at the Center of the Boston Manhunt? | publisher = The Atlantic | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/who-is-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-boston/64382/ | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref> Ethnic [[Chechens]] from the [[North Caucasus]], the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.<ref name="NYTimes04192013" /><ref>{{cite news |url=http://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424127887324493704578432030609754740.html |title=Boston Bombing Suspect Killed in Shootout|date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Wall Street Journal |first1=Evan |last1=Perez |first2=Jennifer |last2=Smith |first3=Pervaiz |last3=Shallwani |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html|title=One Boston Bombing Suspect Is Dead, Second at Large; Area on Lockdown|date=April 19, 2013|newspaper= The New York Times| first1 =Katharine Q | last1 = Seelye | first2 = Michael | last2 = Cooper}}</ref><ref name="captured">{{cite news|url= http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/ |title= 'Captured!!!' Boston police announce Marathon bombing suspect in custody| first1 = Chelsea J | last1 = Carter | first2 = Gregory ‘Greg’ | last2 = Botelho|date=April 20, 2013|work= [[CNN]]}}</ref>  They had been living in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], for the past ten years.<ref name = "AtlanticWire04192013" />  They had previously lived in [[Tokmok]], [[Kyrgyzstan]], and [[Makhachkala]], [[Dagestan]], [[Russia]].<ref name="WashPost04192013">{{cite web | last = Finn | first = Peter | title =  Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal conflict | publisher = Washington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/details-emerge-on-suspected-boston-bombers/2013/04/19/ef2c2566-a8e4-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_story.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="SullivanAP04192013">{{cite news | last = Sullivan | first = Eileen | title =  Manhunt in Boston after bombing suspect is killed | agency = Associated Press | date = April 19, 2013 | url =  http://apnews.myway.com/article/20130419/DA5OPNCO2.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  Both brothers are [[Muslims]].<ref name="HuffPost04192013">{{cite web | last = Kaleem | first = Jaweed | title = Boston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For Bombing  | publisher = Huffington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/04/19/boston-bombing-suspects-muslim_n_3116299.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="HuffPostNoronha04192013">{{cite web | last = Noronha | first = Charmaine | title = Aunt says US suspect recently became devout Muslim | publisher = Huffington Post | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.huffingtonpost.com/huff-wires/20130419/cn-canada-boston-marathon-suspects-aunt/# | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="NYTimes04192013">{{cite news | last = Goode | first = Erica | title =  Brothers Seen as Good Students and Avid Athletes | publisher = New York Times | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/details-of-tsarnaev-brothers-boston-suspects-emerge.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>

[[Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Boston Marathon bombings)|Tamerlan Tsarnaev]] (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.<ref>{{Citation | newspaper = News | publisher = NBC | place = New York | url = http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Boston-Marathon-Bombing-Suspects-JFK-NYC-Travel-International-203787721.html | title = Boston marathon bombing suspects}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title =Boston manhunt for bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev– live updates|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-mit-police-dead-watertown|accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper= The Guardian | place = UK}}</ref><ref name="AtlanticWire04192013" /><ref name="ForeignPolicy04192013" />  He was born in Russia.<ref name="WPostGowen04192013">{{Citation | last = Gowen | first = Annie | last2 = Horwitz | first2 = Sari | last3 = Markon | first3 = Jerry | title = Boston lockdown lifted; marathon bombing suspect still at large | newspaper = [[Washington Post]] | year = 2013 | date = April 19 | url = http://www.washingtonpost.com/world/national-security/massive-police-operation-under-way-in-boston/2013/04/19/979ec6dc-a8c6-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_print.html | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  He had been arrested in 2009 for [[domestic assault]] and [[Battery (crime)|battery]] after assaulting his girlfriend.<ref name="ForeignPolicy04192013"> {{cite web | last = Kenner | first = David | title = Who Is Tamerlan Tsarnaev | publisher = Foreign Policy | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://blog.foreignpolicy.com/posts/2013/04/19/who_is_tamerlan_tzarnaev? | accessdate = April 19, 2013 }}</ref>  He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a [[Permanent residence (United States)|permanent resident]].<ref name="captured" /> He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."<ref name="AtlanticWire04192013" />

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the [[University of Massachusetts Dartmouth]], with a major in marine biology.<ref name=guard_tsarnaev>{{cite news|title=Dzhokhar Tsarnaev: Boston bombing suspect was pupil at Cambridge high school|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-suspect-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-school| place = UK | newspaper= The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/news/national/boston-marathon-suspects-tamerlan-dzhokhar-tsarnaev-appeared-lead-normal-lives-article-1.1321715|title=Boston Marathon suspects Tamerlan, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev: Brothers appeared to lead normal lives|newspaper=New York Daily News}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.boston.com/metrodesk/2013/04/19/bombing-suspect-attended-umass-dartmouth-prompting-school-closure-college-friend-shocked-charge-boston-marathon-bomber/YcEDA5nvNDi0T1jJTNjKiP/story.html|title=Bombing suspect attended UMass Dartmouth, prompting school closure; college friend shocked by charge he is Boston Marathon bomber|newspaper=boston.com}}</ref>  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.<ref name="WPostGowen04192013" />  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.<ref name="captured" />  On television, his uncle, living in [[Montgomery Village, Maryland]], pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Marathon bombers: suspect Dzhozkar Tsarnaev's uncle Ruslan Tsarni pleads 'turn yourself in'|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/northamerica/usa/10006657/Boston-Marathon-bombers-suspect-Dzhozkar-Tsarnaevs-uncle-Ruslan-Tsarni-pleads-turn-yourself-in.html| place = UK | agency=Associated Press|date=April 19, 2013|work=The Telegraph|publisher=Telegraph Media|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19.<ref name=autogenerated2>{{cite web|title=Bombing suspect surrounded in Watertown|url=http://www.lowellsun.com/breakingnews/ci_23065406/sun-staff-and-news-services|publisher=The Lowell Sun|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web|title=Shots Fired In Watertown (Update: Police Have Suspect In Custody)|url=http://www.mediaite.com/online/breaking-shots-fired-in-watertown/|publisher= Mediaite|accessdate= April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2013/apr/19/boston-mit-police-dead-watertown | title = Boston bomb suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev reportedly taken alive | type = live updates | newspaper = The Guardian | accessdate = April 20, 2013 | year = 2013 | month = Apr}}.</ref>

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects: 26-year-old Tamerlan Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев) and 19-year-old Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев). Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, the two emigrated to the United States in 2002.  They had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev (October 21, 1986 – April 19, 2013) was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in Russia.  He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not a U.S. citizen, but was a permanent resident. He had been quoted as saying, "I don't have a single American friend, I don't understand them."

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (born July 22, 1993) at the time of the incident was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. He was found and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19..
