Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".  Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".  Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown, Massachusetts resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".  Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown, Massachusetts resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013.. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology.  He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

On April 18, in a 5:20 p.m. news conference the FBI released photos and a video of two suspects, and sought the public's help in identifying them. The FBI said that one of the suspects had been seen placing a backpack at the bombing scene minutes before the second bomb exploded. Jeff Bauman, who lost both legs, said he provided detailed descriptions to authorities of a suspect who left a bag beside him two and a half minutes before the blast.http://www.foxnews.com/us/2013/04/19/bomb-victim-whose-legs-were-blown-off-reportedly-helped-fbi-id-suspect/

Authorities identified two brothers as the suspects:
Tamerlan Tsarnaev, 26-years old, born October 21, 1986 (Cyrillic script: Тамерлан Царнаев)
Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 19-years-old, born July 22, 1993 (Cyrillic script: Джохар Царнаев).

Ethnic Chechens from the North Caucasus, they were born to Anzor and Zubeidat Tsarnaev. The two emigrated to the United States in 2002 and had been living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years.  They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.  Both brothers are Muslims.

Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive manhunt launched in the early hours of April 19.  He was born in the Russian SFSR in the Soviet Union. He was a well-known boxer with two Golden Glove boxing awards. He had been arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend.   He was not an American citizen, but was a US permanent resident.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was injured and taken into federal custody following a standoff on the evening of April 19, 2013.. At the time of the incident, he was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. He was born in Kyrgyzstan.  He became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012.  On television, his uncle, Ruslan Tsarni, living in Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture.wikitext:
[[File:Tamerlan-and-Dzokhar-Tsarnaev-suspect-photos.jpg|thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings]]
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department]] officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven | first = Stephanie|date = April 19, 2013|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url =http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near the [[Stata Center]] (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web| url = http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |publisher=Boston Globe|title= Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1 =Shelley | last1 = Murphy | first2 = Milton J |last2 = Valencia | first3 = Wesley | last3 = Lowery | first4 = Akilah | last4 = Johnson | first5 = Eric | last5 = Moskowitz | first6 = Lisa | last6 = Wangsness | first7 = John R | last7 = Ellement}}; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url = http://emergency.mit.net/emergency | publisher = MIT | title = Emergency Information | date = April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref name = SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye | first1 = Katherine Q | last2 = Cooper | first2 = Michael|date= April 19, 2013|  work = The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.<ref>{{cite web|last=Finn|first=Peter|title=Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal Chechen conflict|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/details-emerge-on-suspected-boston-bombers/2013/04/19/ef2c2566-a8e4-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_story.html|publisher=''The Washington Post''|accessdate=April 20, 2013|coauthors=Carol D. Leonnig and Will Englund|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times |author=Seelye, K. Q.; Rashbaum, W. K. and Cooper, M.|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to [[Watertown, Massachusetts]].<ref name="captured" /> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html?partner=rss&emc=rss&smid=tw-nytimes |title=Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times | date = April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard.<ref>{{cite web| year = 2013 | month = Apr | url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title=An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston | first =Adam Clark | last = Estes | publisher = The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded.<ref name=nytdragnet/> One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-22212946|title=Boston Marathon bomb suspect still at large|publisher=''[[BBC]]''|date=April 20, 2013|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/|title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ]]|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and was taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html|title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect|publisher=''[[The Boston Globe]]''|first1=Kay|last1=Lazar|first2=Martine|last2=Powers|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury.<ref name=nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan|first1=Eileen |last2=Barr |first2=Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie | agency = Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher=[[WGGB-TV]] |date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 | work =[[The Times]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect",<ref name="CBS April 19">{{cite news| publisher =CBS | agency = Associated Press | title = 1 Boston bombing suspect dead; massive manhunt for 2nd, the "white hat" suspect|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-201_162-57580380/1boston-bombings-suspect-dead-massive-manhunt-for-2nd-the-white-hat-suspect/ | accessdate=April 19, 2013|newspaper=CBS News|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> or "suspect 2", was "still at large".<ref name="Fox19Bombing">{{cite web|url =http://www.fox19.com/story/22020717/gunman-arrested-in-boston-suburb-after-shootout-fbi-on-scene |title=One Boston Marathon bombing suspect is dead, another on the run |date=April 19, 2013|work=[[Fox 19]]|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Early on April 19, Watertown residents received [[reverse 911]] calls asking them to stay indoors.<ref>{{Cite web| url = http://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/watertown/2013/04/officials_in_watertown_field_c.html | year = 2013 | month = Apr | title = Officials in Watertown field calls from worried residents – Watertown – Your Town | newspaper = Boston}}.</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in [[Dagestan]], encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{Cite web | date = April 19, 2013 | url = http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ | title = Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies | publisher = ABC | newspaper = News | accessdate = April 19, 2013}}</ref> [[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=(7) IEDs have been recovered|url=http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/|publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
thumb|right|200px|right|Tamerlan (left) and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (right), the two brothers, suspected of being behind the Boston Marathon bombings
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013 when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns ([[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]], [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]], and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan International Airport]] remained open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry,<ref>{{cite news|title=Boston Bomb Suspect Captured Alive in Backyard Boat|url=http://abcnews.go.com/US/one-boston-marathon-suspect-dead-second-run-police-say/story?id=18994511|author=Thomas, Pierre; Ross, Brian; Ferran, Lee; Curry, Colleen|date=April 19, 2013|work=ABC News|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St.<ref>{{cite news|title=Second Boston Marathon bombing suspect in custody|url=http://www.wcvb.com/Second-Boston-Marathon-bombing-suspect-in-custody/-/9849586/19814816/-/cw8b4az/-/index.html|date=April 20, 2013|work=WCBV.com|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police.<ref>{{cite news|title=Watertown family finds alleged marathon bomber in boat|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/watertown-family-finds-alleged-marathon-bomber-boat/y3te9bJyaatLpd4yvLGRGJ/story.html|author=Anderson, Derek J.|date=April 19, 2013|work=Boston Globe|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through [[thermal imaging]] cameras.<ref name="captured" /> He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff,<ref name=autogenerated2 /><ref name=autogenerated1 /> and transported to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]] where he was listed in [[serious condition]].<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17823265-we-got-him-boston-bombing-suspect-captured-alive | title = 'We got him!': Boston bombing suspect captured alive | place = US | newspaper = News | publisher = NBC | date = 2013‐4‐19}}.</ref>

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a [[Miranda warning]], as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "[[public safety exception]]".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2013/04/next-for-bombing-suspect-high-value-detainee-interrogation-group/ |title=Feds Make Miranda Rights Exception for Marathon Bombing Suspect Dzhokhar Tsarnaev |work=[[ABC News]] |date=April 19, 2013 }}</ref>
Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

(Marathon Bomber)| publisher=YouTube/CNN| date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Three other people were reportedly taken into custody at the housing complex where Dzhokhar Tsarnaev lived.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.masslive.com/news/index.ssf/2013/04/reports_police_arrest_3_in_new.html| title=Police take 3 into custody in New Bedford at housing complex where Boston bombing suspect may have lived| publisher=MassLive.com| date=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the suspects' photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, two suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects had told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception".

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, two suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat that was trailered in his backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception". United States Senators Lindsey Graham and John McCain suggested that Tsarnaev, a U.S. citizen, should be tried as unlawful enemy combatant rather than criminal, preventing him from appointment of counsel.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, two suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. The second suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, sometimes referred to as the "white-hat suspect", or "suspect 2", was "still at large". Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat that was trailered in his backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception". United States Senators Lindsey Graham and John McCain suggested that Tsarnaev, a U.S. citizen, should be tried as unlawful enemy combatant rather than criminal, preventing him from appointment of counsel.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, two suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in a backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception". United States Senators Lindsey Graham and John McCain suggested that Tsarnaev, a U.S. citizen, should be tried as unlawful enemy combatant rather than criminal, preventing him from appointment of counsel.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, two people inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

The suspects next carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached.  The suspects told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and automatic weapon fire heard. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the two suspects exchanging gunfire with police and throwing a bomb at them, which exploded. One suspect, Tamerlan, was captured; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape either in the SUV or by foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was described as "remain[ing] in stable condition".

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors..

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, Anzor Tsarnaev, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the plastic cover of a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in a backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner, David Henneberry, when, shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order was rescinded, Henneberry stepped outside of his home at 67 Franklin St. in Watertown and noticed that the tarp covering the boat was loose, and the cords securing the tarp had been cut. When Henneberry lifted the tarp and looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood, and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence was later verified through thermal imaging cameras. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff, and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center where he was listed in serious condition..

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev has not been read a Miranda warning, as federal law enforcement officials are invoking the "public safety exception". United States Senators Lindsey Graham and John McCain suggested that Tsarnaev, a U.S. citizen, should be tried as unlawful enemy combatant rather than criminal, preventing him from appointment of counsel.
