One perpetrator, allegedly Tamerlan, approached police, ran out of ammunition and was tackled and captured by police officers; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away and driving over his brother. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.
thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in a backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted in Watertown and noticed that the cover covering the boat was cut. When the boat's owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. 

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle which the police used to track the vehicle.  The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard.  It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan, approached police, ran out of ammunition and was tackled and captured by police officers; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away and driving over his brother. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."  NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.
thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in a backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted in Watertown and noticed that the cover covering the boat was cut. When the boat's owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).; originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. 

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle which the police used to track the vehicle.  The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard.  It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. One perpetrator, allegedly Tamerlan, approached police, ran out of ammunition and was tackled and captured by police officers; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away and driving over his brother. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."  NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.
thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in a backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted in Watertown and noticed that the cover covering the boat was cut. When the boat's owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. 

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle which the police used to track the vehicle.  The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.  Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard.  It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. One perpetrator, allegedly Tamerlan, approached police, ran out of ammunition and was tackled and captured by police officers; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away and driving over his brother. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."  NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.
thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in a backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted in Watertown and noticed that the cover covering the boat was cut. When the boat's owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. 

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle which the police used to track the vehicle.  The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.  Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard.  It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged.  Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. One perpetrator, allegedly Tamerlan, approached police, ran out of ammunition and was tackled and captured by police officers; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away and driving over his brother.  He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in  critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."  NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.
thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in a backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted in Watertown and noticed that the cover covering the boat was cut. When the boat's owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."  NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under the tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in a backyard. He was discovered by the boat's owner when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted in Watertown and noticed that the cover covering the boat was cut. When the boat's owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. 

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it.  The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.  Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard.  It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged.  Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. One perpetrator, allegedly Tamerlan, approached police, ran out of ammunition and was tackled and captured by police officers; the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away and driving over his brother.  He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in  critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."  NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. 

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.  They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it.  The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts.  Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard.  It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged.  Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. One perpetrator, allegedly Tamerlan, approached police, ran out of ammunition and was tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and draged him a short distance down the street.  He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in  critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."  NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. One perpetrator, allegedly Tamerlan, approached police, came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Suspects background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived amongst the small Chechen diaspora there. However, according to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. However, reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring talented boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport, training at the Wai Kru Mixed Martial Arts Center, a Lowell club. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. According to a 2010 photo essay about him published by Johannes Hirn in The Comment, the graduate student magazine of Boston University's College of Communications, Tamerlan declared that he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the US Olympic boxing team. He added that he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn’t understand" Americans and had no American friends.

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he became a “follower of radical Islam,” but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. He was a permanent resident but not a citizen of the United States. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christiantiy to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter. Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive exchange of gunfire and explosives in the early hours of April 19.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was seriously injured during a firefight with police in the early hours of April 19 and later taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of the same day.

Suspects background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived amongst the small Chechen diaspora there. However, according to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. However, reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring talented boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport, training at the Wai Kru Mixed Martial Arts Center, a Lowell club. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. According to a 2010 photo essay about him published by Johannes Hirn in The Comment, the graduate student magazine of Boston University's College of Communications, Tamerlan declared that he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the US Olympic boxing team. He added that he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn’t understand" Americans and had no American friends.

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he became a “follower of radical Islam,” but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. He was a permanent resident but not a citizen of the United States. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christiantiy to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter. Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive exchange of gunfire and explosives in the early hours of April 19.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was seriously injured during a firefight with police in the early hours of April 19 and later taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of the same day.

Manhunt and capture.wikitext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department]] officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven |first=Stephanie |date=April 19, 2013|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near the [[Stata Center]] (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web| url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |work= Boston Globe|title=Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1=Shelley |last1=Murphy |first2=Milton J |last2=Valencia |first3=Wesley |last3=Lowery |first4=Akilah |last4=Johnson |first5=Eric |last5=Moskowitz |first6=Lisa |last6=Wangsness |first7=John R |last7=Ellement}} Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://emergency.mit.net/emergency |publisher=MIT |title=Emergency Information |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye |first1=Katherine Q |last2=Cooper |first2=Michael|date= April 19, 2013| work=The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Officer Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash.<ref>{{cite web|last1 =Finn|first1 =Peter|title=Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal Chechen conflict|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/details-emerge-on-suspected-boston-bombers/2013/04/19/ef2c2566-a8e4-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_story.html|work=The Washington Post|accessdate=April 20, 2013| first2 =Carol D |last2=Leonnig |first3=Will |last3=Englund|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to [[Mobile phone tracking|track]] it.<ref name=cnnpol/> The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all |newspaper=The New York Times |last1=Seelye |first1=Katherine Q |last2=Rashbaum |first2=William K |last3=Cooper |first3=Michael |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Police chased the vehicle to [[Watertown, Massachusetts]].<ref name="captured">{{cite news|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/ |title='Captured!!!' Boston police announce Marathon bombing suspect in custody |first1=Chelsea J |last1=Carter |first2=Gregory ‘Greg’ |last2=Botelho |date= April 20, 2013 |publisher=CNN}}</ref> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html |title= Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times |date=April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged.<ref>{{cite web |year=2013 |month=Apr |url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title= An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston |first=Adam Clark |last=Estes |publisher=The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Later in the night, ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them.<ref name=nytdragnet/> One perpetrator, allegedly Tamerlan, approached police, came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street.<ref name=cnnpol>{{cite news|title=Police chief: Boston manhunt began with intense firefight in dark street| publisher= CNN|date= April 20, 2013 |url=http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-details/}}</ref> He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot.<ref name=cnnpol /><ref name=nytdragnet /><ref>{{cite news|url= http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-22212946 |title =Boston Marathon bomb suspect still at large |publisher=BBC|date=April 20, 2013 |accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr.,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/ |title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ-TV|WBZ]]| date =April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded, and was taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he was in [[Medical state#Other terms |critical but stable condition]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html |title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect |work=[[Boston Globe]]|first1= Kay| last1= Lazar |first2=Martine |last2= Powers |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury,<ref name= nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan|first1=Eileen |last2= Barr |first2= Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie |agency=Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher =[[WGGB-TV]] |date= April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.<ref>{{Citation |title=Boston blasts: bomb suspect drove over brother, police say |newspaper=Straits times |date=2013‐4‐21 |url=http://www.straitstimes.com/breaking-news/world/story/boston-blasts-bomb-suspect-drove-over-brother-police-say-20130421}}.</ref> The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web |url =http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 |work =[[The Times]] |place=UK |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Early on April 19, Watertown residents received [[reverse 911]] calls asking them to stay indoors.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/watertown/2013/04/officials_in_watertown_field_c.html |year=2013 |month=Apr |title=Officials in Watertown field calls from worried residents – Watertown – Your Town |newspaper=Boston}}</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in [[Dagestan]], encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{cite web |date=April 19, 2013 |url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ |title=Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies |publisher=ABC |newspaper=News |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> [[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title= Seven IEDs have been recovered|url= http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/ |publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title= Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:MissionHillCaptureCelebrations.jpg|thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy [[Mission Hill, Boston|Mission Hill]] neighborhood.]]

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. Police chased the vehicle to Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. Later in the night, The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. One perpetrator, allegedly Tamerlan, approached police, came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. A transit police officer, identified as 33-year-old Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr., was critically wounded, and was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19). Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Suspects background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived amongst the small Chechen diaspora there. However, according to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. However, reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring talented boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport, training at the Wai Kru Mixed Martial Arts Center, a Lowell club. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. According to a 2010 photo essay about him published by Johannes Hirn in The Comment, the graduate student magazine of Boston University's College of Communications, Tamerlan declared that he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the US Olympic boxing team. He added that he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn’t understand" Americans and had no American friends.

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he became a “follower of radical Islam,” but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. He was a permanent resident but not a citizen of the United States. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christiantiy to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter. Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive exchange of gunfire and explosives in the early hours of April 19.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was seriously injured during a firefight with police in the early hours of April 19 and later taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of the same day.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarp covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Suspects background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived among the small Chechen diaspora there. However, according to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. However, reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring talented boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport, training at the Wai Kru Mixed Martial Arts Center, a Lowell club. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. According to a 2010 photo essay about him published by Johannes Hirn in The Comment, the graduate student magazine of Boston University's College of Communications, Tamerlan declared that he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the US Olympic boxing team. He added that he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn’t understand" Americans and had no American friends.

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he became a “follower of radical Islam,” but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. He was a permanent resident but not a citizen of the United States. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christiantiy to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter. Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive exchange of gunfire and explosives in the early hours of April 19.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was seriously injured during a firefight with police in the early hours of April 19 and later taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of the same day.

The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web |url =http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 |work =[[The Times]] |place=UK |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Early on April 19, Watertown residents received [[reverse 911]] calls asking them to stay indoors.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/watertown/2013/04/officials_in_watertown_field_c.html |year=2013 |month=Apr |title=Officials in Watertown field calls from worried residents – Watertown – Your Town |newspaper=Boston}}</ref>

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.

After this murder, the perpetrators carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge and forced the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two suspects during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarpaulin covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside of his home shortly after the "shelter-in-place" order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a human form lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Suspects background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived among the small Chechen diaspora there. However, according to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. However, reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring talented boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport, training at the Wai Kru Mixed Martial Arts Center, a Lowell club. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. He was a permanent resident of the United States. According to a 2010 photo essay about him published by Johannes Hirn in The Comment, the graduate student magazine of Boston University's College of Communications, Tamerlan declared that he was working to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the US Olympic boxing team. He added that he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn’t understand" Americans and had no American friends.

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he became a “follower of radical Islam,” but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christiantiy to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter. Tamerlan Tsarnaev was killed during a massive exchange of gunfire and explosives in the early hours of April 19.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was seriously injured during a firefight with police in the early hours of April 19 and later taken into federal custody following a standoff in the evening of the same day.
