Suspects' background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived among the small Chechen diaspora there. According to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. Reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. He was a permanent resident of the United States and hoped to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native Chechnya becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.

Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he became a "follower of radical Islam," but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. In late 2012 after returning from Russia, Tamerlan's life took on an "increasingly puritanical religious tone" with "Islamist certainty." He appeared, to some family members, to become an "extremist."

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christianity to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture.wikitext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department]] officer from [[Somerville, Massachusetts]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Officer killed in MIT standoff identified as Sean Collier, 26| last =Haven |first= Stephanie |date=April 19, 2013|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|publisher=Gannett|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url= http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/04/19/boston-mit-officer-collier/2096329/}}</ref> who was seated in his police car on the campus of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], near the [[Stata Center]] (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).<ref name="lowery">{{cite web| url= http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/18/mit-police-officer-hit-gunfire-cambridge-police-dispatcher-says/4UeCClOVeLr8PHLvDa99zK/story.html |work= Boston Globe|title=Search for marathon bombing suspect locks down Watertown, surrounding communities|date= April 19, 2013|accessdate= April 19, 2013| first1=Shelley |last1= Murphy |first2=Milton J |last2=Valencia |first3=Wesley |last3=Lowery |first4=Akilah |last4=Johnson |first5 = Eric |last5=Moskowitz |first6=Lisa |last6=Wangsness |first7=John R |last7=Ellement}}  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting".</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://emergency.mit.net/emergency |publisher=MIT |title=Emergency Information |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19>{{cite news| title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose| last1 =Seelye |first1=Katherine Q |last2=Cooper |first2=Michael|date= April 19, 2013| work=The New York Times|accessdate=April 19, 2013|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=2&hp&pagewanted=all}}</ref> Officer Collier was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead.<ref name=SeelyeCooper-nyt19 /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/local/10010403717086/police-mit-police-officer-fatally-shot-gunman-sought|publisher=WHDH|title=Police: MIT police officer fatally shot, gunman sought|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> The suspects then [[carjacking|carjacked]] a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge, forcing the owner to use his [[ATM card]] to obtain $800 in cash.<ref>{{cite web|last1 =Finn|first1 =Peter|title=Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal Chechen conflict|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/details-emerge-on-suspected-boston-bombers/2013/04/19/ef2c2566-a8e4-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_story.html|work=The Washington Post|accessdate=April 20, 2013| first2 =Carol D |last2=Leonnig |first3=Will |last3=Englund|date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached, but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to [[Mobile phone tracking|track]] it.<ref name=cnnpol/> The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing.<ref name= nytdragnet>{{cite news |title= Dragnet Shuts Boston; One Suspect Is Slain but Second Man Is on Loose|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html?pagewanted=3&_r=0&pagewanted=all |newspaper=The New York Times |last1=Seelye |first1=Katherine Q |last2=Rashbaum |first2=William K |last3=Cooper |first3=Michael |date=April 19, 2013}}</ref> 

Police located the stolen SUV in [[Watertown, Massachusetts]].<ref name="captured">{{cite news|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/ |title='Captured!!!' Boston police announce Marathon bombing suspect in custody |first1=Chelsea J |last1=Carter |first2=Gregory ‘Greg’ |last2=Botelho |date= April 20, 2013 |publisher=CNN}}</ref> Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/explosives-detonated-in-massachusetts-standoff.html |title= Explosives Detonated in Massachusetts Standoff |newspaper=The New York Times |date=April 20, 2013}}</ref> with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged.<ref>{{cite web |year=2013 |month=Apr |url=http://www.theatlanticwire.com/national/2013/04/theres-shooter-loose-and-officer-down-mit/64379/ |title= An Officer's Been Killed and There's a Shooter on the Loose in Boston |first=Adam Clark |last=Estes |publisher=The Atlantic Wire |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings.<ref name="lowery" /> A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them.<ref name=nytdragnet/> Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street.<ref name=cnnpol>{{cite news|title=Police chief: Boston manhunt began with intense firefight in dark street| publisher= CNN|date= April 20, 2013 |url=http://www.cnn.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-details/}}</ref> He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot.<ref name=cnnpol /><ref name=nytdragnet /><ref>{{cite news|url= http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-22212946 |title =Boston Marathon bomb suspect still at large |publisher=BBC|date=April 20, 2013 |accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> During the firefight, 33-year-old [[MBTA]] Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://boston.cbslocal.com/2013/04/19/mbta-police-officer-shot-while-chasing-suspects/ |title=MBTA Police Officer Shot While Chasing Bombing Suspects|publisher=[[WBZ-TV|WBZ]]| date =April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> was critically wounded. He was taken to [[Mount Auburn Hospital]], where he was in [[Medical state#Other terms|critical but stable condition]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/massachusetts/2013/04/19/mbta-officer-wounded-boston-bomb-suspect-chase-known-neighbors-devoted-dad/I6ti0qf5iSnXGeVszGpTxI/story.html |title=MBTA officer wounded in shoot-out with bombing suspect |work=[[Boston Globe]]|first1= Kay| last1= Lazar |first2=Martine |last2= Powers |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to [[Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center]], where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury,<ref name= nytdragnet/><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-police-issue-fresh-photo-of-suspect-2/ |last1=Sullivan|first1=Eileen |last2= Barr |first2= Meghan |last3=Zezima |first3=Katie |agency=Associated Press |title=Boston Bombing Suspect ID’ed as Cambridge Man |publisher =[[WGGB-TV]] |date= April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.<ref>{{Citation |title=Boston blasts: bomb suspect drove over brother, police say |newspaper=Straits times |date=2013‐4‐21 |url=http://www.straitstimes.com/breaking-news/world/story/boston-blasts-bomb-suspect-drove-over-brother-police-say-20130421}}.</ref> 

The FBI released additional photos of the two during the Watertown incident.<ref name="Philippe Naughton">{{cite web |url =http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/americas/article3743697.ece|title= Live: Boston bomb suspect killed by police, one hunted|last= Naughton|first= Philippe|date= April 19, 2013 |work =[[The Times]] |place=UK |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> Early on April 19, Watertown residents received [[reverse 911]] calls asking them to stay indoors.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.boston.com/yourtown/news/watertown/2013/04/officials_in_watertown_field_c.html |year=2013 |month=Apr |title=Officials in Watertown field calls from worried residents – Watertown – Your Town |newspaper=Boston}}</ref>

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in [[Makhachkala]] in [[Dagestan]], encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia."<ref>{{cite web |date=April 19, 2013 |url=http://www.wggb.com/2013/04/19/boston-suspects-father-dzhokhar-is-a-true-angel/ |title=Boston Bomb Suspect’s Dad Tells Him to Surrender, Warns ‘Hell Will Break Loose’ if Son Dies |publisher=ABC |newspaper=News |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> [[NBC News]] reports seven [[Improvised explosive device|IED]]s were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web|title= Seven IEDs have been recovered|url= http://inagist.com/all/325341152335257600/ |publisher=Inigist|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title= Evening thread: Cops continue to hunt Tsarnaev; Update: Seven IEDs recovered|url=http://hotair.com/archives/2013/04/19/evening-thread-cops-continue-to-hunt-tsarnaev/|publisher=Hotair|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

[[File:MissionHillCaptureCelebrations.jpg|thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy [[Mission Hill, Boston|Mission Hill]] neighborhood.]]
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor [[Deval Patrick]] asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, [[Belmont, Massachusetts|Belmont]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Newton, Massachusetts|Newton]], and [[Waltham, Massachusetts|Waltham]]<ref name="Boston stay-in-place">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/04/19/metropolitan-boston-awakens-under-siege-police-launch-manhunt-for-marathon-bomber/AcObNkQ5NOJC4Acv2azyZJ/story.html |title= Boston-area residents urged to remain indoors| date=April 19, 2013 | newspaper =Boston Globe |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>) to "[[shelter in place]]". The entire [[Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority|public transit network]] as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was [[Amtrak]] service to and from Boston.<ref name="lowery" /><ref name="Logan and Taxis" /> [[Logan International Airport]] remained open.<ref name="Logan and Taxis">{{cite news |url= http://www.usatoday.com/story/todayinthesky/2013/04/19/boston-flights-operating-but-under-heightened-security/2096217/ |title=Boston flights operating, airlines waive change fees |first=Ben |last=Mutzabaugh |date=April 19, 2013 |accessdate=April 19, 2013 |newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a [[tarpaulin]] covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts, who was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge, forcing the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached, but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarpaulin covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside his home shortly after the shelter-in-place order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a body lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Suspects' background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived among the small Chechen diaspora there. According to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. Reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. He was a permanent resident of the United States and hoped to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native Chechnya becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.

Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he became a "follower of radical Islam," but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. In late 2012 after returning from Russia, Tamerlan's life took on an "increasingly puritanical religious tone" with "Islamist certainty." He appeared, to some family members, to become an "extremist."

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christianity to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts,, he was the brother of Hendrick Motorsports machinist Andrew CollierNASCAR - For Hendrick team, Boston attacks hit home.  Sean was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge, forcing the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached, but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarpaulin covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside his home shortly after the shelter-in-place order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a body lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts; he was the brother of Hendrick Motorsports machinist Andrew Collier.NASCAR - For Hendrick team, Boston attacks hit home  Sean was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge, forcing the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached, but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarpaulin covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside his home shortly after the shelter-in-place order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a body lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition.

Their parents also have two daughters. Suspects' background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived among the small Chechen diaspora there. According to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. Reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. He was a permanent resident of the United States and hoped to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native Chechnya becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.

Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he became a "follower of radical Islam," but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. In late 2012 after returning from Russia, Tamerlan's life took on an "increasingly puritanical religious tone" with "Islamist certainty." He appeared, to some family members, to become an "extremist."

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christianity to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

He was a permanent resident of the United States and hoped to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native Chechnya becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.

Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he became a "follower of radical Islam," but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. In late 2012 after returning from Russia, Tamerlan's life took on an "increasingly puritanical religious tone" with "Islamist certainty." He appeared, to some family members, to become an "extremist."

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christianity to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Suspects' background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived among the small Chechen diaspora there. According to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. Reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for  refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. He was a permanent resident of the United States and hoped to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native Chechnya becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.

Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian  Federal Security Service that he became a "follower of radical Islam," but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. In late 2012 after returning from Russia, Tamerlan's life took on an "increasingly puritanical religious tone" with "Islamist certainty." He appeared, to some family members, to become an "extremist."

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christianity to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts. Sean was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge, forcing the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached, but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to give up peacefully: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarpaulin covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside his home shortly after the shelter-in-place order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a body lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition. According to authorities, Tsarnaev apparently tried to kill himself, judging by the gunshot wound to his neck.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts. Sean was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge, forcing the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached, but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to try to flee the country: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarpaulin covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside his home shortly after the shelter-in-place order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a body lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition. According to authorities, Tsarnaev apparently tried to kill himself, judging by the gunshot wound to his neck.

Suspects' background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived among the small Chechen diaspora there. According to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. Reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for  refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. He was a permanent resident of the United States and hoped to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native Chechnya becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.

Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian  Federal Security Service that he became a "follower of radical Islam," but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. In late 2012 after returning from Russia, Tamerlan's life took on an "increasingly puritanical religious tone" with "Islamist certainty." He appeared, to some family members, to become an "extremist."

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christianity to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Suspects' background.plaintext:
The brothers are ethnic Chechens and Muslims. Their places of birth are disputed. Kyrgyz police claim that both brothers were born in Kyrgyzstan, while their families lived among the small Chechen diaspora there. According to the extended Tsarnaev family in the United States, the younger brother, Dzhokhar, was born in Dagestan, Russia. Reports in the U.S. media suggest the opposite: that Dzhokhar was born in Kyrgyzstan while Tamerlan was born in the Russian SFSR.

Their parents also have two daughters. The entire Tsarnaev family, including both brothers, immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for  refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer. An aspiring boxer, he dropped out of school to concentrate on his sport. In 2010 he was the New England Golden Gloves heavyweight champion and won the Rocky Marciano Trophy. He was a permanent resident of the United States and hoped to become a naturalized citizen in time to be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native Chechnya becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia", though stating that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.

Tamerlan, in the last three years, became more devout and religious, with a growing Salafist and radical viewpoint. The FBI was informed by the Russian  Federal Security Service that he became a "follower of radical Islam," but the agency found no evidence of associations with foreign jihadi. In late 2012 after returning from Russia, Tamerlan's life took on an "increasingly puritanical religious tone" with "Islamist certainty." He appeared, to some family members, to become an "extremist."

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. He was married to a U.S. citizen who converted from Christianity to Islam to marry him. The couple have a 3-year-old daughter.

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. He was also an avid wrestler and part of the all-star wrestling team at his school. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts. Sean was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge, forcing the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached, but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to try to flee the country: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." and said that, "“If they killed him, then all hell would break loose.” NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarpaulin covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside his home shortly after the shelter-in-place order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a body lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition. According to authorities, Tsarnaev apparently tried to kill himself, judging by the gunshot wound to his neck.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts. Sean was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge, forcing the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached, but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gun fire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to try to flee the country: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." He continued, "If they killed him, then all hell would break loose.” NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarpaulin covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside his home shortly after the shelter-in-place order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a body lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition. According to authorities, Tsarnaev apparently tried to kill himself, judging by the gunshot wound to his neck.

Suspects' background.wikitext:
Tamerlan was born in 1986 in [[Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic|Russian SFSR]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://usnews.nbcnews.com/_news/2013/04/19/17817173-one-boston-marathon-suspect-killed-second-suspect-his-brother-on-loose-after-firefight#.UXEyGDO7X3c.twitter|title=Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal Chechen conflict|publisher=NBC News|date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=April 21, 2013}}</ref> although authorities in [[Kyrgyzstan]] say he was born there.<ref name="GuardianBirthplace"/> Dzhokhar was born in 1993 in Kyrgyzstan, although his family claims he was born in [[Dagestan]], [[Russia]].<ref name="GuardianBirthplace"/> The brothers spent time in [[Tomok]], Kyrgyzstan. They are [[Muslim]] [[Chechens]],<ref name="NYTimes04192013">{{cite news| last= Goode | first = Erica |title=Brothers Seen as Good Students and Avid Athletes|newspaper= The New York Times |date = April 19, 2013 | url=http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/details-of-tsarnaev-brothers-boston-suspects-emerge.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref name="HuffPost04192013">{{cite news | last = Kaleem| first= Jaweed|title= Boston Bombing Suspects' Muslim Identity Provides Few Clues To Motivation For Bombing |newspaper= Huffington Post|date= April 19, 2013|url= http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/04/19/boston-bombing-suspects-muslim_n_3116299.html |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref name= "HuffPostNoronha04192013">{{cite news|last=Noronha| first=Charmaine|title=Aunt says US suspect recently became devout Muslim|newspaper = Huffington Post|date=April 19, 2013|url= http://www.huffingtonpost.com/huff-wires/20130419/cn-canada-boston-marathon-suspects-aunt/#|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref> though they never lived in [[Chechnya]].<ref name="GuardianBirthplace"/> 	

The Tsarnaev brothers and their family [[Immigration to the United States|immigrated]] in 2002 to the United States,<ref name="captured">{{cite news|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2013/04/19/us/boston-area-violence/ |title= 'Captured!!!' Boston police announce Marathon bombing suspect in custody|first1=Chelsea J|last1=Carter|first2=Gregory ‘Greg’|last2=Botelho|date=April 20, 2013|publisher=CNN}}</ref><ref name="NYTimes04192013"/><ref>{{cite news|url= http://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424127887324493704578432030609754740.html|title=Boston Bombing Suspect Killed in Shootout|date= April 19, 2013|newspaper=The Wall Street Journal|first1=Evan|last1=Perez|first2=Jennifer | last2=Smith|first3 = Pervaiz | last3=Shallwani |accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url = http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/20/us/boston-marathon-bombings.html |title= One Boston Bombing Suspect Is Dead, Second at Large; Area on Lockdown|date =April 19, 2013|newspaper=The New York Times|first1 =Katharine Q|last1= Seelye| first2 = Michael | last2=Cooper}}</ref> where they applied for [[Asylum in the United States| refugee status]] and settled in [[Massachusetts]], with Tamerlan living in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], for the past ten years.<ref name ="AtlanticWire04192013"/> They had previously lived in [[Tokmok]], [[Kyrgyzstan]], and [[Makhachkala]], Dagestan, Russia.<ref name="WashPost04192013">{{cite news|last=Finn|first=Peter|title=Tamerlan Tsarnaev and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev were refugees from brutal conflict|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=April 19, 2013|url = http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/details-emerge-on-suspected-boston-bombers/2013/04/19/ef2c2566-a8e4-11e2-a8e2-5b98cb59187f_story.html|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref><ref name="SullivanAP04192013">{{cite news|last= Sullivan|first=Eileen|title=Manhunt in Boston after bombing suspect is killed|agency=Associated Press|date=April 19, 2013 |url=http://apnews.myway.com/article/20130419/DA5OPNCO2.html|accessdate=April 19, 2013}}</ref>

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended [[Bunker Hill Community College]] with hopes of becoming an engineer, but later dropped out to become a boxer.<ref name="thecomment">{{Citation|last=Hirn|first= Johannes|title=Will box for Passport: An Olympic Drive to become a United States citizen|newspaper =The Comment|year=2010|url= http://www.bu.edu/com/comment/library/downloads/2010_comment.pdf|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref><ref name="deadspin">{{Citation|last=Burke|first=Thimothy |title=Everything we know about Tamerlan Tsarnaev, dead bombing suspect|newspaper= Deadspin|date=April 19, 2013|url= http://deadspin.com/heres-everything-we-know-about-tamerlan-tsarnaev-the-476415081|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> He was a [[Permanent residence (United States)|permanent resident]] of the United States<ref name="captured"/> and hoped to become a naturalized citizen, so that he could be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native [[Chechnya]] becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia".<ref name="thecomment"/><ref name="deadspin"/><ref name="mailonline"/> He was married to a U.S. citizen, and has a daughter,<ref name="mailonline">{{cite web|url=http://www.dailymail.co.uk/news/article-2311809/Tamerlan-Tsarnaev-Boston-bomber-married-Katherine-Russell-converted-Islam-marry-him.html?ITO=1490&ns_mchannel=rss&ns_campaign=1490|title=Our hearts are sickened by the horror he inflicted': Shocked family of All-American girl who converted to Islam to marry Boston bomber say tragedy proves 'we never really knew him|last1=Nathan|first1=Sara| last2=Bates|first2=Daniel|date=April 19, 2013|newspaper=Daily Mail|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref> The couple have a 3-year-old daughter.<ref name="mailonline"/> but stated that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://now.msn.com/tamerlan-tsarnaev-said-he-had-no-american-friends|title=Tamerlan Tsarnaev said he had no American friends|publisher=MSN|accessdate=April 20, 2013}}</ref>

Suspects' background.plaintext:
Tamerlan was born in 1986 in Russian SFSR, although authorities in Kyrgyzstan say he was born there. Dzhokhar was born in 1993 in Kyrgyzstan, although his family claims he was born in Dagestan, Russia. The brothers spent time in Tomok, Kyrgyzstan. They are Muslim Chechens, though they never lived in Chechnya. 	

The Tsarnaev brothers and their family immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for  refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer, but later dropped out to become a boxer. He was a permanent resident of the United States and hoped to become a naturalized citizen, so that he could be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native Chechnya becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia". He was married to a U.S. citizen, and has a daughter, The couple have a 3-year-old daughter. but stated that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. 
The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service that he was a "follower of radical Islam." In response, the FBI interviewed Tamerlan and his family, and searched databases, but did not find any evidence of "terrorism activity, domestic or foreign." 

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.

Manhunt and capture.plaintext:
After the photos were released, the suspects inflicted multiple gunshot wounds on Sean Collier, 26, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology Police Department officer from Somerville, Massachusetts. Sean was seated in his police car on the campus of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, near the Stata Center (Building 32) on April 18 at 10:48 p.m. EDT (02:48 UTC, April 19).  Originally titled "Chaos in Cambridge, Watertown after fatal shooting". Officer Collier was taken to Massachusetts General Hospital in nearby downtown Boston, where he was pronounced dead. The suspects then carjacked a silver Mercedes SUV in Cambridge, forcing the owner to use his ATM card to obtain $800 in cash. They released the man after the ATM cash limit was reached, but his cellphone remained in the vehicle, allowing the police to track it. The carjackers told the man that they were responsible for the Boston bombings and MIT officer killing. 

Police located the stolen SUV in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police in Watertown reported that they exchanged gunfire with two suspects following the MIT shooting, with explosions and much gunfire heard. It was later determined that about 200 rounds were exchanged. The Boston Globe reported that the shooting suspects were the same men being sought in the Marathon bombings. A Watertown resident observed the perpetrators exchanging gunfire with police and throwing explosives at them. Tamerlan came within 5 to 10 feet of the nearest police officer while firing at the officers, before he ran out of ammunition and was subsequently tackled and captured by police officers. At that time the other, Dzhokhar, managed to escape in the SUV, forcing the police officers to dive away while Dzhokhar drove over his brother Tamerlan and dragged him a short distance down the street. He then abandoned the SUV and escaped on foot. During the firefight, 33-year-old MBTA Police Officer Richard H. Donahue Jr. was critically wounded. He was taken to Mount Auburn Hospital, where he was in critical but stable condition.

During the morning of April 19, after the car chase and exchange of fire with law enforcement, Tamerlan Tsarnaev was taken by police to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he died of multiple gunshot wounds and a possible blast injury, as well as injuries sustained due to his brother driving the vehicle over him.. 

The FBI released additional photos of the two during the Watertown incident. Early on April 19, Watertown residents received reverse 911 calls asking them to stay indoors.

Thousands of law enforcement personnel participated in a door-to-door manhunt in Watertown, as well as following up other leads, including at the house the brothers shared in Cambridge. The father of the suspected Boston Marathon bombers, speaking from his home in Makhachkala in Dagestan, encouraged his son to try to flee the country: "Give up. Give up. You have a bright future ahead of you. Come home to Russia." He continued, "If they killed him, then all hell would break loose.” NBC News reports seven IEDs were recovered in the searches so far: some in Watertown and some at the Tsarnaevs' house in Cambridge.

thumb|Post-capture celebrations in Boston's student-heavy Mission Hill neighborhood.
On the morning of April 19, Massachusetts Governor Deval Patrick asked residents of Watertown and adjacent cities and towns (Boston, Belmont, Brookline, Cambridge, Newton, and Waltham) to "shelter in place". The entire public transit network as well as most Boston taxi service was suspended, as was Amtrak service to and from Boston. Logan International Airport remained open. Universities, schools, many businesses, and other facilities were closed.

The manhunt ended on the evening of April 19, 2013, when authorities surrounded Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who had taken refuge under a tarpaulin covering a Watertown resident's boat that was on a trailer in his backyard. He was discovered when the boat's owner stepped outside his home shortly after the shelter-in-place order had been lifted and noticed that the boat's cover was cut. When the owner looked into the boat, he saw a body lying in a pool of blood and promptly notified police. Tsarnaev's presence and movement was later verified through a thermal imaging device in a State Police helicopter. He was taken into custody around 8:42 p.m. EDT after a standoff and transported to Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, where he was listed in serious condition. According to authorities, Tsarnaev apparently tried to kill himself, judging by the gunshot wound to his neck.

Suspects' background.plaintext:
Tamerlan was born in 1986 in Russian SFSR, although authorities in Kyrgyzstan say he was born there. Dzhokhar was born in 1993 in Kyrgyzstan, although his family claims he was born in Dagestan, Russia. The brothers spent time in Tomok, Kyrgyzstan. They are Muslim Chechens, though they never lived in Chechnya. 	

The Tsarnaev brothers and their family immigrated in 2002 to the United States, where they applied for  refugee status and settled in Massachusetts, with Tamerlan living in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for the past ten years. They had previously lived in Tokmok, Kyrgyzstan, and Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.

After arriving in the United States in 2002, Tamerlan Tsarnaev attended Bunker Hill Community College with hopes of becoming an engineer, but later dropped out to become a boxer. He was a permanent resident of the United States and hoped to become a naturalized citizen, so that he could be selected for the U.S. Olympic boxing team. He added that "unless his native Chechnya becomes independent" he would "rather compete for the United States than for Russia". He was married to a U.S. citizen, and has a daughter, The couple have a 3-year-old daughter. but stated that he "didn't understand" Americans and had no American friends.

He was arrested in 2009 for domestic assault and battery after allegedly assaulting his girlfriend. 
The FBI was informed by the Russian Federal Security Service in 2011 that he was a "follower of radical Islam." In response, the FBI interviewed Tamerlan and his family, and searched databases, but did not find any evidence of "terrorism activity, domestic or foreign." 

At the time of the bombing, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was a student at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, with a major in marine biology. Dzhokhar became a naturalized U.S. citizen on September 11, 2012. Tamerlan's boxing coach, John Curran reported to NBC that "the young brother was like a puppy dog following his older brother". On television, his uncle from Montgomery Village, Maryland, pleaded with Dzhokhar to turn himself in.
